- **PR #**: 1290
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1290
- **Title**: fix(1252): widen scheduled-indicator reminder window past loaded-runner pre-check
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1252-followup-row-order` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +15
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:45:45Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T20:57:04Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1252

## Root cause (artifact-backed, FILE:LINE)
`test/integration/scheduled_indicator_test.dart` scripts a `schedule_message` with `delay: 20s`, then asserts the `⏰ 1 scheduled · next in` ETA inside a 10s `waitForScreen` that starts only after boot + scheduling turn + settle waits. On loaded CI runners that pre-check path measured **~44 s**: the CI dart-test JSON artifact of failing run 37223287603 (integration-json-shard-0) shows the test starting at suite-t=171.5 s and erroring at 225.5 s (54 s total), with the TimeoutException from `pty_harness.dart:377 waitForScreen` ← `scheduled_indicator_test.dart:64` (`· next in`). The failure screen already shows the complete fire→wake→deliver lifecycle (`[sched] fired:`, `[btw] mail → complete`, row cleared) — the record's 20 s pending window expired before the ETA check began sampling.

Product code audited and correct in all three artifacts: queue math (`scheduled_messages.dart` `dueMs`, `_armAsync` timer legs, boot re-arm via `start()`), sweep paths (`agent_cli_inbox.dart` `deliverDue` at boot/turn/wake), row renderer (`fa_tui_rows.dart:407 _scheduledRowLine`, epoch-millisecond ETA, minute-boundary repaint via `fa_tui.dart:819 _scheduleScheduledTick`). This is the same window-budget class as gh-1012; that fix's premise ("schedule → indicator → turn-complete tail is then a bounded ~2s") no longer holds on today's runners.

## Change (test-only, 15+/9−)
- Scripted reminder delay `20s` → `90s`: the pending window now dwarfs the worst observed pre-check path (~44 s) with ~2× headroom, so the `· next in` samples always land on a live record.
- Corrected the stale header comment (bounded-tail premise) and mock doc (said "3s delay"); documented the 44 s artifact measurement inline.
- All downstream budgets still line up: 10 s ETA wait samples ~46+ s before the fire; 90 s `[sched] fired:` wait covers the new fire point; 45 s clear poll and 5 m file timeout unchanged.

## Delivered vs remaining
- Delivered: window-budget fix + evidence-linked comments; no product code touched.
- Remaining: none known.

## Gates (disclosure)
Targeted `dart analyze` could not run on this box (shared Flutter SDK cache is read-only for the agent — wrapper fails before analyze starts; per lane policy the single attempt was spent, no dart test attempted — box runs a live LLM loop). Edits are string-literal/comment-only in one test file. **PR CI is the real gate.**

## Quarantine (`scripts/test_quarantine.json`)
Entry for this file/test **stays** in this PR, per gh-1199 AC4: the gate runs it supervised, nightly must produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof on the fixed code before removal (flakes are timing-dependent; a green repeat has not been produced yet). Please review/keep the entry as merged by #1249.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1290
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1290
- **Title**: fix(1252): widen scheduled-indicator reminder window past loaded-runner pre-check
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1252-followup-row-order` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +15
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:45:45Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T20:57:04Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1252

## Root cause (artifact-backed, FILE:LINE)
`test/integration/scheduled_indicator_test.dart` scripts a `schedule_message` with `delay: 20s`, then asserts the `⏰ 1 scheduled · next in` ETA inside a 10s `waitForScreen` that starts only after boot + scheduling turn + settle waits. On loaded CI runners that pre-check path measured **~44 s**: the CI dart-test JSON artifact of failing run 37223287603 (integration-json-shard-0) shows the test starting at suite-t=171.5 s and erroring at 225.5 s (54 s total), with the TimeoutException from `pty_harness.dart:377 waitForScreen` ← `scheduled_indicator_test.dart:64` (`· next in`). The failure screen already shows the complete fire→wake→deliver lifecycle (`[sched] fired:`, `[btw] mail → complete`, row cleared) — the record's 20 s pending window expired before the ETA check began sampling.

Product code audited and correct in all three artifacts: queue math (`scheduled_messages.dart` `dueMs`, `_armAsync` timer legs, boot re-arm via `start()`), sweep paths (`agent_cli_inbox.dart` `deliverDue` at boot/turn/wake), row renderer (`fa_tui_rows.dart:407 _scheduledRowLine`, epoch-millisecond ETA, minute-boundary repaint via `fa_tui.dart:819 _scheduleScheduledTick`). This is the same window-budget class as gh-1012; that fix's premise ("schedule → indicator → turn-complete tail is then a bounded ~2s") no longer holds on today's runners.

## Change (test-only, 15+/9−)
- Scripted reminder delay `20s` → `90s`: the pending window now dwarfs the worst observed pre-check path (~44 s) with ~2× headroom, so the `· next in` samples always land on a live record.
- Corrected the stale header comment (bounded-tail premise) and mock doc (said "3s delay"); documented the 44 s artifact measurement inline.
- All downstream budgets still line up: 10 s ETA wait samples ~46+ s before the fire; 90 s `[sched] fired:` wait covers the new fire point; 45 s clear poll and 5 m file timeout unchanged.

## Delivered vs remaining
- Delivered: window-budget fix + evidence-linked comments; no product code touched.
- Remaining: none known.

## Gates (disclosure)
Targeted `dart analyze` could not run on this box (shared Flutter SDK cache is read-only for the agent — wrapper fails before analyze starts; per lane policy the single attempt was spent, no dart test attempted — box runs a live LLM loop). Edits are string-literal/comment-only in one test file. **PR CI is the real gate.**

## Quarantine (`scripts/test_quarantine.json`)
Entry for this file/test **stays** in this PR, per gh-1199 AC4: the gate runs it supervised, nightly must produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof on the fixed code before removal (flakes are timing-dependent; a green repeat has not been produced yet). Please review/keep the entry as merged by #1249.

- **Title**: fix(1252): widen scheduled-indicator reminder window past loaded-runner pre-check
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1252-followup-row-order` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +15
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:45:45Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T20:57:04Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1252

## Root cause (artifact-backed, FILE:LINE)
`test/integration/scheduled_indicator_test.dart` scripts a `schedule_message` with `delay: 20s`, then asserts the `⏰ 1 scheduled · next in` ETA inside a 10s `waitForScreen` that starts only after boot + scheduling turn + settle waits. On loaded CI runners that pre-check path measured **~44 s**: the CI dart-test JSON artifact of failing run 37223287603 (integration-json-shard-0) shows the test starting at suite-t=171.5 s and erroring at 225.5 s (54 s total), with the TimeoutException from `pty_harness.dart:377 waitForScreen` ← `scheduled_indicator_test.dart:64` (`· next in`). The failure screen already shows the complete fire→wake→deliver lifecycle (`[sched] fired:`, `[btw] mail → complete`, row cleared) — the record's 20 s pending window expired before the ETA check began sampling.

Product code audited and correct in all three artifacts: queue math (`scheduled_messages.dart` `dueMs`, `_armAsync` timer legs, boot re-arm via `start()`), sweep paths (`agent_cli_inbox.dart` `deliverDue` at boot/turn/wake), row renderer (`fa_tui_rows.dart:407 _scheduledRowLine`, epoch-millisecond ETA, minute-boundary repaint via `fa_tui.dart:819 _scheduleScheduledTick`). This is the same window-budget class as gh-1012; that fix's premise ("schedule → indicator → turn-complete tail is then a bounded ~2s") no longer holds on today's runners.

## Change (test-only, 15+/9−)
- Scripted reminder delay `20s` → `90s`: the pending window now dwarfs the worst observed pre-check path (~44 s) with ~2× headroom, so the `· next in` samples always land on a live record.
- Corrected the stale header comment (bounded-tail premise) and mock doc (said "3s delay"); documented the 44 s artifact measurement inline.
- All downstream budgets still line up: 10 s ETA wait samples ~46+ s before the fire; 90 s `[sched] fired:` wait covers the new fire point; 45 s clear poll and 5 m file timeout unchanged.

## Delivered vs remaining
- Delivered: window-budget fix + evidence-linked comments; no product code touched.
- Remaining: none known.

## Gates (disclosure)
Targeted `dart analyze` could not run on this box (shared Flutter SDK cache is read-only for the agent — wrapper fails before analyze starts; per lane policy the single attempt was spent, no dart test attempted — box runs a live LLM loop). Edits are string-literal/comment-only in one test file. **PR CI is the real gate.**

## Quarantine (`scripts/test_quarantine.json`)
Entry for this file/test **stays** in this PR, per gh-1199 AC4: the gate runs it supervised, nightly must produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof on the fixed code before removal (flakes are timing-dependent; a green repeat has not been produced yet). Please review/keep the entry as merged by #1249.

# pr-1290: fix(1252): widen scheduled-indicator reminder window past loaded-runner pre-check

## Description

Fixes #1252

## Root cause (artifact-backed, FILE:LINE)
`test/integration/scheduled_indicator_test.dart` scripts a `schedule_message` with `delay: 20s`, then asserts the `⏰ 1 scheduled · next in` ETA inside a 10s `waitForScreen` that starts only after boot + scheduling turn + settle waits. On loaded CI runners that pre-check path measured **~44 s**: the CI dart-test JSON artifact of failing run 37223287603 (integration-json-shard-0) shows the test starting at suite-t=171.5 s and erroring at 225.5 s (54 s total), with the TimeoutException from `pty_harness.dart:377 waitForScreen` ← `scheduled_indicator_test.dart:64` (`· next in`). The failure screen already shows the complete fire→wake→deliver lifecycle (`[sched] fired:`, `[btw] mail → complete`, row cleared) — the record's 20 s pending window expired before the ETA check began sampling.

Product code audited and correct in all three artifacts: queue math (`scheduled_messages.dart` `dueMs`, `_armAsync` timer legs, boot re-arm via `start()`), sweep paths (`agent_cli_inbox.dart` `deliverDue` at boot/turn/wake), row renderer (`fa_tui_rows.dart:407 _scheduledRowLine`, epoch-millisecond ETA, minute-boundary repaint via `fa_tui.dart:819 _scheduleScheduledTick`). This is the same window-budget class as gh-1012; that fix's premise ("schedule → indicator → turn-complete tail is then a bounded ~2s") no longer holds on today's runners.

## Change (test-only, 15+/9−)
- Scripted reminder delay `20s` → `90s`: the pending window now dwarfs the worst observed pre-check path (~44 s) with ~2× headroom, so the `· next in` samples always land on a live record.
- Corrected the stale header comment (bounded-tail premise) and mock doc (said "3s delay"); documented the 44 s artifact measurement inline.
- All downstream budgets still line up: 10 s ETA wait samples ~46+ s before the fire; 90 s `[sched] fired:` wait covers the new fire point; 45 s clear poll and 5 m file timeout unchanged.

## Delivered vs remaining
- Delivered: window-budget fix + evidence-linked comments; no product code touched.
- Remaining: none known.

## Gates (disclosure)
Targeted `dart analyze` could not run on this box (shared Flutter SDK cache is read-only for the agent — wrapper fails before analyze starts; per lane policy the single attempt was spent, no dart test attempted — box runs a live LLM loop). Edits are string-literal/comment-only in one test file. **PR CI is the real gate.**

## Quarantine (`scripts/test_quarantine.json`)
Entry for this file/test **stays** in this PR, per gh-1199 AC4: the gate runs it supervised, nightly must produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof on the fixed code before removal (flakes are timing-dependent; a green repeat has not been produced yet). Please review/keep the entry as merged by #1249.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1290
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1290
- **Title**: fix(1252): widen scheduled-indicator reminder window past loaded-runner pre-check
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1252-followup-row-order` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +15
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:45:45Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T20:57:04Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1252

## Root cause (artifact-backed, FILE:LINE)
`test/integration/scheduled_indicator_test.dart` scripts a `schedule_message` with `delay: 20s`, then asserts the `⏰ 1 scheduled · next in` ETA inside a 10s `waitForScreen` that starts only after boot + scheduling turn + settle waits. On loaded CI runners that pre-check path measured **~44 s**: the CI dart-test JSON artifact of failing run 37223287603 (integration-json-shard-0) shows the test starting at suite-t=171.5 s and erroring at 225.5 s (54 s total), with the TimeoutException from `pty_harness.dart:377 waitForScreen` ← `scheduled_indicator_test.dart:64` (`· next in`). The failure screen already shows the complete fire→wake→deliver lifecycle (`[sched] fired:`, `[btw] mail → complete`, row cleared) — the record's 20 s pending window expired before the ETA check began sampling.

Product code audited and correct in all three artifacts: queue math (`scheduled_messages.dart` `dueMs`, `_armAsync` timer legs, boot re-arm via `start()`), sweep paths (`agent_cli_inbox.dart` `deliverDue` at boot/turn/wake), row renderer (`fa_tui_rows.dart:407 _scheduledRowLine`, epoch-millisecond ETA, minute-boundary repaint via `fa_tui.dart:819 _scheduleScheduledTick`). This is the same window-budget class as gh-1012; that fix's premise ("schedule → indicator → turn-complete tail is then a bounded ~2s") no longer holds on today's runners.

## Change (test-only, 15+/9−)
- Scripted reminder delay `20s` → `90s`: the pending window now dwarfs the worst observed pre-check path (~44 s) with ~2× headroom, so the `· next in` samples always land on a live record.
- Corrected the stale header comment (bounded-tail premise) and mock doc (said "3s delay"); documented the 44 s artifact measurement inline.
- All downstream budgets still line up: 10 s ETA wait samples ~46+ s before the fire; 90 s `[sched] fired:` wait covers the new fire point; 45 s clear poll and 5 m file timeout unchanged.

## Delivered vs remaining
- Delivered: window-budget fix + evidence-linked comments; no product code touched.
- Remaining: none known.

## Gates (disclosure)
Targeted `dart analyze` could not run on this box (shared Flutter SDK cache is read-only for the agent — wrapper fails before analyze starts; per lane policy the single attempt was spent, no dart test attempted — box runs a live LLM loop). Edits are string-literal/comment-only in one test file. **PR CI is the real gate.**

## Quarantine (`scripts/test_quarantine.json`)
Entry for this file/test **stays** in this PR, per gh-1199 AC4: the gate runs it supervised, nightly must produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof on the fixed code before removal (flakes are timing-dependent; a green repeat has not been produced yet). Please review/keep the entry as merged by #1249.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1290
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1290
- **Title**: fix(1252): widen scheduled-indicator reminder window past loaded-runner pre-check
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1252-followup-row-order` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +15
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:45:45Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T20:57:04Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1252

## Root cause (artifact-backed, FILE:LINE)
`test/integration/scheduled_indicator_test.dart` scripts a `schedule_message` with `delay: 20s`, then asserts the `⏰ 1 scheduled · next in` ETA inside a 10s `waitForScreen` that starts only after boot + scheduling turn + settle waits. On loaded CI runners that pre-check path measured **~44 s**: the CI dart-test JSON artifact of failing run 37223287603 (integration-json-shard-0) shows the test starting at suite-t=171.5 s and erroring at 225.5 s (54 s total), with the TimeoutException from `pty_harness.dart:377 waitForScreen` ← `scheduled_indicator_test.dart:64` (`· next in`). The failure screen already shows the complete fire→wake→deliver lifecycle (`[sched] fired:`, `[btw] mail → complete`, row cleared) — the record's 20 s pending window expired before the ETA check began sampling.

Product code audited and correct in all three artifacts: queue math (`scheduled_messages.dart` `dueMs`, `_armAsync` timer legs, boot re-arm via `start()`), sweep paths (`agent_cli_inbox.dart` `deliverDue` at boot/turn/wake), row renderer (`fa_tui_rows.dart:407 _scheduledRowLine`, epoch-millisecond ETA, minute-boundary repaint via `fa_tui.dart:819 _scheduleScheduledTick`). This is the same window-budget class as gh-1012; that fix's premise ("schedule → indicator → turn-complete tail is then a bounded ~2s") no longer holds on today's runners.

## Change (test-only, 15+/9−)
- Scripted reminder delay `20s` → `90s`: the pending window now dwarfs the worst observed pre-check path (~44 s) with ~2× headroom, so the `· next in` samples always land on a live record.
- Corrected the stale header comment (bounded-tail premise) and mock doc (said "3s delay"); documented the 44 s artifact measurement inline.
- All downstream budgets still line up: 10 s ETA wait samples ~46+ s before the fire; 90 s `[sched] fired:` wait covers the new fire point; 45 s clear poll and 5 m file timeout unchanged.

## Delivered vs remaining
- Delivered: window-budget fix + evidence-linked comments; no product code touched.
- Remaining: none known.

## Gates (disclosure)
Targeted `dart analyze` could not run on this box (shared Flutter SDK cache is read-only for the agent — wrapper fails before analyze starts; per lane policy the single attempt was spent, no dart test attempted — box runs a live LLM loop). Edits are string-literal/comment-only in one test file. **PR CI is the real gate.**

## Quarantine (`scripts/test_quarantine.json`)
Entry for this file/test **stays** in this PR, per gh-1199 AC4: the gate runs it supervised, nightly must produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof on the fixed code before removal (flakes are timing-dependent; a green repeat has not been produced yet). Please review/keep the entry as merged by #1249.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1290
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1290
- **Title**: fix(1252): widen scheduled-indicator reminder window past loaded-runner pre-check
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1252-followup-row-order` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +15
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:45:45Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T20:57:04Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1252

## Root cause (artifact-backed, FILE:LINE)
`test/integration/scheduled_indicator_test.dart` scripts a `schedule_message` with `delay: 20s`, then asserts the `⏰ 1 scheduled · next in` ETA inside a 10s `waitForScreen` that starts only after boot + scheduling turn + settle waits. On loaded CI runners that pre-check path measured **~44 s**: the CI dart-test JSON artifact of failing run 37223287603 (integration-json-shard-0) shows the test starting at suite-t=171.5 s and erroring at 225.5 s (54 s total), with the TimeoutException from `pty_harness.dart:377 waitForScreen` ← `scheduled_indicator_test.dart:64` (`· next in`). The failure screen already shows the complete fire→wake→deliver lifecycle (`[sched] fired:`, `[btw] mail → complete`, row cleared) — the record's 20 s pending window expired before the ETA check began sampling.

Product code audited and correct in all three artifacts: queue math (`scheduled_messages.dart` `dueMs`, `_armAsync` timer legs, boot re-arm via `start()`), sweep paths (`agent_cli_inbox.dart` `deliverDue` at boot/turn/wake), row renderer (`fa_tui_rows.dart:407 _scheduledRowLine`, epoch-millisecond ETA, minute-boundary repaint via `fa_tui.dart:819 _scheduleScheduledTick`). This is the same window-budget class as gh-1012; that fix's premise ("schedule → indicator → turn-complete tail is then a bounded ~2s") no longer holds on today's runners.

## Change (test-only, 15+/9−)
- Scripted reminder delay `20s` → `90s`: the pending window now dwarfs the worst observed pre-check path (~44 s) with ~2× headroom, so the `· next in` samples always land on a live record.
- Corrected the stale header comment (bounded-tail premise) and mock doc (said "3s delay"); documented the 44 s artifact measurement inline.
- All downstream budgets still line up: 10 s ETA wait samples ~46+ s before the fire; 90 s `[sched] fired:` wait covers the new fire point; 45 s clear poll and 5 m file timeout unchanged.

## Delivered vs remaining
- Delivered: window-budget fix + evidence-linked comments; no product code touched.
- Remaining: none known.

## Gates (disclosure)
Targeted `dart analyze` could not run on this box (shared Flutter SDK cache is read-only for the agent — wrapper fails before analyze starts; per lane policy the single attempt was spent, no dart test attempted — box runs a live LLM loop). Edits are string-literal/comment-only in one test file. **PR CI is the real gate.**

## Quarantine (`scripts/test_quarantine.json`)
Entry for this file/test **stays** in this PR, per gh-1199 AC4: the gate runs it supervised, nightly must produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof on the fixed code before removal (flakes are timing-dependent; a green repeat has not been produced yet). Please review/keep the entry as merged by #1249.

Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] CI -->|No| THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix
— cover the exact scenario called out (including boundary/multi-item cases, not just the happy path)"] T2["GREEN: Make the minimum code change to turn the test PASS
— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1290
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1290
- **Title**: fix(1252): widen scheduled-indicator reminder window past loaded-runner pre-check
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1252-followup-row-order` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +15
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:45:45Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T20:57:04Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1252

## Root cause (artifact-backed, FILE:LINE)
`test/integration/scheduled_indicator_test.dart` scripts a `schedule_message` with `delay: 20s`, then asserts the `⏰ 1 scheduled · next in` ETA inside a 10s `waitForScreen` that starts only after boot + scheduling turn + settle waits. On loaded CI runners that pre-check path measured **~44 s**: the CI dart-test JSON artifact of failing run 37223287603 (integration-json-shard-0) shows the test starting at suite-t=171.5 s and erroring at 225.5 s (54 s total), with the TimeoutException from `pty_harness.dart:377 waitForScreen` ← `scheduled_indicator_test.dart:64` (`· next in`). The failure screen already shows the complete fire→wake→deliver lifecycle (`[sched] fired:`, `[btw] mail → complete`, row cleared) — the record's 20 s pending window expired before the ETA check began sampling.

Product code audited and correct in all three artifacts: queue math (`scheduled_messages.dart` `dueMs`, `_armAsync` timer legs, boot re-arm via `start()`), sweep paths (`agent_cli_inbox.dart` `deliverDue` at boot/turn/wake), row renderer (`fa_tui_rows.dart:407 _scheduledRowLine`, epoch-millisecond ETA, minute-boundary repaint via `fa_tui.dart:819 _scheduleScheduledTick`). This is the same window-budget class as gh-1012; that fix's premise ("schedule → indicator → turn-complete tail is then a bounded ~2s") no longer holds on today's runners.

## Change (test-only, 15+/9−)
- Scripted reminder delay `20s` → `90s`: the pending window now dwarfs the worst observed pre-check path (~44 s) with ~2× headroom, so the `· next in` samples always land on a live record.
- Corrected the stale header comment (bounded-tail premise) and mock doc (said "3s delay"); documented the 44 s artifact measurement inline.
- All downstream budgets still line up: 10 s ETA wait samples ~46+ s before the fire; 90 s `[sched] fired:` wait covers the new fire point; 45 s clear poll and 5 m file timeout unchanged.

## Delivered vs remaining
- Delivered: window-budget fix + evidence-linked comments; no product code touched.
- Remaining: none known.

## Gates (disclosure)
Targeted `dart analyze` could not run on this box (shared Flutter SDK cache is read-only for the agent — wrapper fails before analyze starts; per lane policy the single attempt was spent, no dart test attempted — box runs a live LLM loop). Edits are string-literal/comment-only in one test file. **PR CI is the real gate.**

## Quarantine (`scripts/test_quarantine.json`)
Entry for this file/test **stays** in this PR, per gh-1199 AC4: the gate runs it supervised, nightly must produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof on the fixed code before removal (flakes are timing-dependent; a green repeat has not been produced yet). Please review/keep the entry as merged by #1249.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1290
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1290
- **Title**: fix(1252): widen scheduled-indicator reminder window past loaded-runner pre-check
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1252-followup-row-order` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +15
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:45:45Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T20:57:04Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1252

## Root cause (artifact-backed, FILE:LINE)
`test/integration/scheduled_indicator_test.dart` scripts a `schedule_message` with `delay: 20s`, then asserts the `⏰ 1 scheduled · next in` ETA inside a 10s `waitForScreen` that starts only after boot + scheduling turn + settle waits. On loaded CI runners that pre-check path measured **~44 s**: the CI dart-test JSON artifact of failing run 37223287603 (integration-json-shard-0) shows the test starting at suite-t=171.5 s and erroring at 225.5 s (54 s total), with the TimeoutException from `pty_harness.dart:377 waitForScreen` ← `scheduled_indicator_test.dart:64` (`· next in`). The failure screen already shows the complete fire→wake→deliver lifecycle (`[sched] fired:`, `[btw] mail → complete`, row cleared) — the record's 20 s pending window expired before the ETA check began sampling.

Product code audited and correct in all three artifacts: queue math (`scheduled_messages.dart` `dueMs`, `_armAsync` timer legs, boot re-arm via `start()`), sweep paths (`agent_cli_inbox.dart` `deliverDue` at boot/turn/wake), row renderer (`fa_tui_rows.dart:407 _scheduledRowLine`, epoch-millisecond ETA, minute-boundary repaint via `fa_tui.dart:819 _scheduleScheduledTick`). This is the same window-budget class as gh-1012; that fix's premise ("schedule → indicator → turn-complete tail is then a bounded ~2s") no longer holds on today's runners.

## Change (test-only, 15+/9−)
- Scripted reminder delay `20s` → `90s`: the pending window now dwarfs the worst observed pre-check path (~44 s) with ~2× headroom, so the `· next in` samples always land on a live record.
- Corrected the stale header comment (bounded-tail premise) and mock doc (said "3s delay"); documented the 44 s artifact measurement inline.
- All downstream budgets still line up: 10 s ETA wait samples ~46+ s before the fire; 90 s `[sched] fired:` wait covers the new fire point; 45 s clear poll and 5 m file timeout unchanged.

## Delivered vs remaining
- Delivered: window-budget fix + evidence-linked comments; no product code touched.
- Remaining: none known.

## Gates (disclosure)
Targeted `dart analyze` could not run on this box (shared Flutter SDK cache is read-only for the agent — wrapper fails before analyze starts; per lane policy the single attempt was spent, no dart test attempted — box runs a live LLM loop). Edits are string-literal/comment-only in one test file. **PR CI is the real gate.**

## Quarantine (`scripts/test_quarantine.json`)
Entry for this file/test **stays** in this PR, per gh-1199 AC4: the gate runs it supervised, nightly must produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof on the fixed code before removal (flakes are timing-dependent; a green repeat has not been produced yet). # pr-1290: fix(1252): widen scheduled-indicator reminder window past loaded-runner pre-check

## Description

Fixes #1252

## Root cause (artifact-backed, FILE:LINE)
`test/integration/scheduled_indicator_test.dart` scripts a `schedule_message` with `delay: 20s`, then asserts the `⏰ 1 scheduled · next in` ETA inside a 10s `waitForScreen` that starts only after boot + scheduling turn + settle waits. On loaded CI runners that pre-check path measured **~44 s**: the CI dart-test JSON artifact of failing run 37223287603 (integration-json-shard-0) shows the test starting at suite-t=171.5 s and erroring at 225.5 s (54 s total), with the TimeoutException from `pty_harness.dart:377 waitForScreen` ← `scheduled_indicator_test.dart:64` (`· next in`). The failure screen already shows the complete fire→wake→deliver lifecycle (`[sched] fired:`, `[btw] mail → complete`, row cleared) — the record's 20 s pending window expired before the ETA check began sampling.

Product code audited and correct in all three artifacts: queue math (`scheduled_messages.dart` `dueMs`, `_armAsync` timer legs, boot re-arm via `start()`), sweep paths (`agent_cli_inbox.dart` `deliverDue` at boot/turn/wake), row renderer (`fa_tui_rows.dart:407 _scheduledRowLine`, epoch-millisecond ETA, minute-boundary repaint via `fa_tui.dart:819 _scheduleScheduledTick`). This is the same window-budget class as gh-1012; that fix's premise ("schedule → indicator → turn-complete tail is then a bounded ~2s") no longer holds on today's runners.

## Change (test-only, 15+/9−)
- Scripted reminder delay `20s` → `90s`: the pending window now dwarfs the worst observed pre-check path (~44 s) with ~2× headroom, so the `· next in` samples always land on a live record.
- Corrected the stale header comment (bounded-tail premise) and mock doc (said "3s delay"); documented the 44 s artifact measurement inline.
- All downstream budgets still line up: 10 s ETA wait samples ~46+ s before the fire; 90 s `[sched] fired:` wait covers the new fire point; 45 s clear poll and 5 m file timeout unchanged.

## Delivered vs remaining
- Delivered: window-budget fix + evidence-linked comments; no product code touched.
- Remaining: none known.

## Gates (disclosure)
Targeted `dart analyze` could not run on this box (shared Flutter SDK cache is read-only for the agent — wrapper fails before analyze starts; per lane policy the single attempt was spent, no dart test attempted — box runs a live LLM loop). Edits are string-literal/comment-only in one test file. **PR CI is the real gate.**

## Quarantine (`scripts/test_quarantine.json`)
Entry for this file/test **stays** in this PR, per gh-1199 AC4: the gate runs it supervised, nightly must produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof on the fixed code before removal (flakes are timing-dependent; a green repeat has not been produced yet). Please review/keep the entry as merged by #1249.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1290
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1290
- **Title**: fix(1252): widen scheduled-indicator reminder window past loaded-runner pre-check
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1252-followup-row-order` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +15
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:45:45Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T20:57:04Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1252

## Root cause (artifact-backed, FILE:LINE)
`test/integration/scheduled_indicator_test.dart` scripts a `schedule_message` with `delay: 20s`, then asserts the `⏰ 1 scheduled · next in` ETA inside a 10s `waitForScreen` that starts only after boot + scheduling turn + settle waits. On loaded CI runners that pre-check path measured **~44 s**: the CI dart-test JSON artifact of failing run 37223287603 (integration-json-shard-0) shows the test starting at suite-t=171.5 s and erroring at 225.5 s (54 s total), with the TimeoutException from `pty_harness.dart:377 waitForScreen` ← `scheduled_indicator_test.dart:64` (`· next in`). The failure screen already shows the complete fire→wake→deliver lifecycle (`[sched] fired:`, `[btw] mail → complete`, row cleared) — the record's 20 s pending window expired before the ETA check began sampling.

Product code audited and correct in all three artifacts: queue math (`scheduled_messages.dart` `dueMs`, `_armAsync` timer legs, boot re-arm via `start()`), sweep paths (`agent_cli_inbox.dart` `deliverDue` at boot/turn/wake), row renderer (`fa_tui_rows.dart:407 _scheduledRowLine`, epoch-millisecond ETA, minute-boundary repaint via `fa_tui.dart:819 _scheduleScheduledTick`). This is the same window-budget class as gh-1012; that fix's premise ("schedule → indicator → turn-complete tail is then a bounded ~2s") no longer holds on today's runners.

## Change (test-only, 15+/9−)
- Scripted reminder delay `20s` → `90s`: the pending window now dwarfs the worst observed pre-check path (~44 s) with ~2× headroom, so the `· next in` samples always land on a live record.
- Corrected the stale header comment (bounded-tail premise) and mock doc (said "3s delay"); documented the 44 s artifact measurement inline.
- All downstream budgets still line up: 10 s ETA wait samples ~46+ s before the fire; 90 s `[sched] fired:` wait covers the new fire point; 45 s clear poll and 5 m file timeout unchanged.

## Delivered vs remaining
- Delivered: window-budget fix + evidence-linked comments; no product code touched.
- Remaining: none known.

## Gates (disclosure)
Targeted `dart analyze` could not run on this box (shared Flutter SDK cache is read-only for the agent — wrapper fails before analyze starts; per lane policy the single attempt was spent, no dart test attempted — box runs a live LLM loop). Edits are string-literal/comment-only in one test file. **PR CI is the real gate.**

## Quarantine (`scripts/test_quarantine.json`)
Entry for this file/test **stays** in this PR, per gh-1199 AC4: the gate runs it supervised, nightly must produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof on the fixed code before removal (flakes are timing-dependent; a green repeat has not been produced yet). Please review/keep the entry as merged by #1249.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1290
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1290
- **Title**: fix(1252): widen scheduled-indicator reminder window past loaded-runner pre-check
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1252-followup-row-order` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +15
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:45:45Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T20:57:04Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1252

## Root cause (artifact-backed, FILE:LINE)
`test/integration/scheduled_indicator_test.dart` scripts a `schedule_message` with `delay: 20s`, then asserts the `⏰ 1 scheduled · next in` ETA inside a 10s `waitForScreen` that starts only after boot + scheduling turn + settle waits. On loaded CI runners that pre-check path measured **~44 s**: the CI dart-test JSON artifact of failing run 37223287603 (integration-json-shard-0) shows the test starting at suite-t=171.5 s and erroring at 225.5 s (54 s total), with the TimeoutException from `pty_harness.dart:377 waitForScreen` ← `scheduled_indicator_test.dart:64` (`· next in`). The failure screen already shows the complete fire→wake→deliver lifecycle (`[sched] fired:`, `[btw] mail → complete`, row cleared) — the record's 20 s pending window expired before the ETA check began sampling.

Product code audited and correct in all three artifacts: queue math (`scheduled_messages.dart` `dueMs`, `_armAsync` timer legs, boot re-arm via `start()`), sweep paths (`agent_cli_inbox.dart` `deliverDue` at boot/turn/wake), row renderer (`fa_tui_rows.dart:407 _scheduledRowLine`, epoch-millisecond ETA, minute-boundary repaint via `fa_tui.dart:819 _scheduleScheduledTick`). This is the same window-budget class as gh-1012; that fix's premise ("schedule → indicator → turn-complete tail is then a bounded ~2s") no longer holds on today's runners.

## Change (test-only, 15+/9−)
- Scripted reminder delay `20s` → `90s`: the pending window now dwarfs the worst observed pre-check path (~44 s) with ~2× headroom, so the `· next in` samples always land on a live record.
- Corrected the stale header comment (bounded-tail premise) and mock doc (said "3s delay"); documented the 44 s artifact measurement inline.
- All downstream budgets still line up: 10 s ETA wait samples ~46+ s before the fire; 90 s `[sched] fired:` wait covers the new fire point; 45 s clear poll and 5 m file timeout unchanged.

## Delivered vs remaining
- Delivered: window-budget fix + evidence-linked comments; no product code touched.
- Remaining: none known.

## Gates (disclosure)
Targeted `dart analyze` could not run on this box (shared Flutter SDK cache is read-only for the agent — wrapper fails before analyze starts; per lane policy the single attempt was spent, no dart test attempted — box runs a live LLM loop). Edits are string-literal/comment-only in one test file. **PR CI is the real gate.**

## Quarantine (`scripts/test_quarantine.json`)
Entry for this file/test **stays** in this PR, per gh-1199 AC4: the gate runs it supervised, nightly must produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof on the fixed code before removal (flakes are timing-dependent; a green repeat has not been produced yet). Please review/keep the entry as merged by #1249.

blocks.text:
Now I understand the flake:

The test runs ten background bash jobs: `sleep ${2 + i} && echo p573-job-$i` for i=1..10, so sleeps are 3..12 seconds.

Then at line ~157:
```dart
final settledNumbers = _settleNotice
    .allMatches(drained)
    .map((m) => m.group(1)!.split('-').first)
    .toSet();
expect(
  settledNumbers,
  {for (var i = 1; i <= 10; i++) '$i'},
  ...
);
```

`_settleNotice = RegExp(r'\[bash\] sh-(\S+) exited\(0\)')` — matches `[bash] sh-<id> exited(0)` settle notices.

The failure: `settledNumbers` = {1,2,3,4} (missing 5..10) in run 37527310604, and {1..7} (missing 8,9,10) in run 37517510546.

So only the first 4 (or 7) jobs produced settle notices by the time `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500, timeout: 60s)` returned. Wait, but the timeout is 60s and jobs sleep 3..12s. How could only 4 finish in 60s? Unless `waitForOutput` returned early — it returns when output is "settled" (no new output for settleMs=500ms). Hmm, but settle notices keep streaming every ~1s as jobs finish (staggered 3..12s, so ~1s apart). If waitForOutput returns on a 500ms settle gap, it could return early between notices... but jobs finish ~1s apart, so there shouldn't be a 500ms gap...

Actually wait — look at the ordering: jobs launch staggered? All ten bash jobs launch essentially at the same time (10 tool calls in one turn). Sleeps: 3,4,5,...,12s. So finish events happen at ~3s, ~4s, ~5s, ..., ~12s — one per second. With settleMs: 500, waitForOutput would return only after a 500ms gap with no output... which never happens while jobs are finishing 1s apart. UNLESS output events are batched differently.

Hmm, but the failure shows waitForOutput returned after only 4 settle notices (t≈3,4,5,6 → returns at ~6.5s? Or the notices for 4 jobs). Under heavy CI load, jobs run slowly; sleeps don't depend on CPU though. BUT the notice delivery may be batched: the TUI delivers settle notices on frame repaints. If the terminal is busy, multiple notices could be coalesced into one frame and then... the regex captures distinct numbers; missing ones mean they never appeared in the drained stream.

Wait — actually, re-read the comment in the test:

"Frame repaints re-emit notices into the raw stream — the start/finish proof is the set of DISTINCT settled job numbers, not the raw match count."

So `drained` = the raw output stream chunk returned by waitForOutput. The notices are re-emitted on repaints. Missing numbers → the notices weren't emitted (yet) when waitForOutput returned.

Why would waitForOutput return before all 10 jobs finished? Because `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500)` returns when the output stream is quiet for 500ms. Between t=6s (job 4 done) and t=7s (job 5 done) there's a 1s gap... that's > 500ms! So waitForOutput CAN return in any of those ~1s gaps. That's exactly the bug: with staggered sleeps 3..12 (1s apart), the inter-notice gap is ~1s ≥ 500ms settle window, so `waitForOutput` can return after ANY notice, e.g. after the 4th.

Hmm wait, but then this test would be flaky by design... unless normally PTY output repaints keep the stream busy during the whole drain (status line repaints every second via countdown tick etc.). Actually the board counts down each second (`9 running`, `8 running`...), which repaints frames, generating output. The settle notices themselves are emitted... let me think.

Actually the "0 running" wait later would still pass since drain completes by ~12s. And the settledNumbers set built from `drained` (just the final waitForOutput chunk?) — if the chunk only covers part of the drain, numbers missing.

Hold on — let me check `waitForOutput` in pty_harness.dart to understand exactly what it returns. Also, does it accumulate the whole stream or just the final chunk?

Also — the timing: in the failing CI run, the failure happened at 20:35:32, and the test group started at 20:35:13.7 (after lsp_dart_server_test at 20:35:13). So the failing test ran 20:34:57 → 20:35:32 (~35s) roughly. The ten sleeps take max 12s. Under load, more.

Key question: why did the drain stop after job 4? Look at the actual timeline:
- If the ten bash jobs start at T0 (after the turn's tool calls all spawn), sleeps end at T0+3..T0+12.
- `waitForScreen(_allRunning, 60s)` — waits for "10 running".
- `waitForOutput(settleMs: 200)`.
- mid-flight loop until a count in 1..9 appears (up to 60s).
- `waitForOutput(settleMs: 200)`.
- `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500, timeout: 60s)` → returns `drained` — this is the window where notices must all appear.

If between two notices there's ≥500ms of silence, waitForOutput returns early. Sleeps are 1s apart, so with NO repaint noise in between, a 500ms window WILL expire between notices. But the countdown board repaints every... the countdown tick? The board shows "N running" which changes when a job finishes — that's event-driven, not a 1Hz tick. So between job 4 finishing at T+6 and job 5 at T+7, is there any other output? Probably not! So waitForOutput(settleMs: 500) would return at ~T+6.5s, with only 4 notices. That matches {1,2,3,4} exactly!

Hmm wait, but then this test would fail almost EVERY time... but it passes usually ("116 tests passed, 1 failed"). Something else must normally generate output. Let me check waitForOutput's implementation — maybe it drains the ACCUMULATED stream since its last call, and the settle window starts from the last output... Let me read pty_harness.dart.

Also there's a "settle-notice run" — "A settle-notice run (the async-result flow) streams between settles — the board keeps counting down across runs." The turn ends, then settle notices for finished jobs spawn NEW runs ("[bash] sh-… exited(0)" as mail). Each settle notice triggers a new turn/run (the async-result flow). So after the main turn ends, each job finish triggers a run that streams the notice.

Let me read the harness and understand. Then check whether there's a known fix approach — maybe gh-1337 issue was auto-filed for v1.0.520's red, and a fix is expected in this rework? Wait, careful: my primary job is the PR rework for PR #1290 (fix #1252). The CI failure (shell_job_countdown flake) is blocking the PR's validation. The instructions say: fix CI root cause.

The failure exists on main too (v1.0.520 tag run 37517510546 failed with the same test). So it's not caused by the PR. But the PR can't go green while this test fails on the shared CI. Options:
1. Fix the flake in the test (window budget class like gh-1252 — same family).
2. Quarantine the flaky test per the repo's quarantine mechanism (scripts/test_quarantine.json), like previous flakes (flake-quarantine/shell_job_countdown_pty branch exists!).

Interesting: there's a branch `flake-quarantine/shell_job_countdown_pty` — meaning this test was quarantined before and later un-quarantined. Let me check the quarantine file history and the AGENTS.md policy on flakes/quarantine.

Now I understand the flake:

The test runs ten background bash jobs: `sleep ${2 + i} && echo p573-job-$i` for i=1..10, so sleeps are 3..12 seconds.

Then at line ~157:
```dart
final settledNumbers = _settleNotice
    .allMatches(drained)
    .map((m) => m.group(1)!.split('-').first)
    .toSet();
expect(
  settledNumbers,
  {for (var i = 1; i <= 10; i++) '$i'},
  ...
);
```

`_settleNotice = RegExp(r'\[bash\] sh-(\S+) exited\(0\)')` — matches `[bash] sh-<id> exited(0)` settle notices.

The failure: `settledNumbers` = {1,2,3,4} (missing 5..10) in run 37527310604, and {1..7} (missing 8,9,10) in run 37517510546.

So only the first 4 (or 7) jobs produced settle notices by the time `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500, timeout: 60s)` returned. Wait, but the timeout is 60s and jobs sleep 3..12s. How could only 4 finish in 60s? Unless `waitForOutput` returned early — it returns when output is "settled" (no new output for settleMs=500ms). Hmm, but settle notices keep streaming every ~1s as jobs finish (staggered 3..12s, so ~1s apart). If waitForOutput returns on a 500ms settle gap, it could return early between notices... but jobs finish ~1s apart, so there shouldn't be a 500ms gap...

Actually wait — look at the ordering: jobs launch staggered? All ten bash jobs launch essentially at the same time (10 tool calls in one turn). Sleeps: 3,4,5,...,12s. So finish events happen at ~3s, ~4s, ~5s, ..., ~12s — one per second. With settleMs: 500, waitForOutput would return only after a 500ms gap with no output... which never happens while jobs are finishing 1s apart. UNLESS output events are batched differently.

Hmm, but the failure shows waitForOutput returned after only 4 settle notices (t≈3,4,5,6 → returns at ~6.5s? Or the notices for 4 jobs). Under heavy CI load, jobs run slowly; sleeps don't depend on CPU though. BUT the notice delivery may be batched: the TUI delivers settle notices on frame repaints. If the terminal is busy, multiple notices could be coalesced into one frame and then... the regex captures distinct numbers; missing ones mean they never appeared in the drained stream.

Wait — actually, re-read the comment in the test:

"Frame repaints re-emit notices into the raw stream — the start/finish proof is the set of DISTINCT settled job numbers, not the raw match count."

So `drained` = the raw output stream chunk returned by waitForOutput. The notices are re-emitted on repaints. Missing numbers → the notices weren't emitted (yet) when waitForOutput returned.

Why would waitForOutput return before all 10 jobs finished? Because `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500)` returns when the output stream is quiet for 500ms. Between t=6s (job 4 done) and t=7s (job 5 done) there's a 1s gap... that's > 500ms! So waitForOutput CAN return in any of those ~1s gaps. That's exactly the bug: with staggered sleeps 3..12 (1s apart), the inter-notice gap is ~1s ≥ 500ms settle window, so `waitForOutput` can return after ANY notice, e.g. after the 4th.

Hmm wait, but then this test would be flaky by design... unless normally PTY output repaints keep the stream busy during the whole drain (status line repaints every second via countdown tick etc.). Actually the board counts down each second (`9 running`, `8 running`...), which repaints frames, generating output. The settle notices themselves are emitted... let me think.

Actually the "0 running" wait later would still pass since drain completes by ~12s. And the settledNumbers set built from `drained` (just the final waitForOutput chunk?) — if the chunk only covers part of the drain, numbers missing.

Hold on — let me check `waitForOutput` in pty_harness.dart to understand exactly what it returns. Also, does it accumulate the whole stream or just the final chunk?

- If the ten bash jobs start at T0 (after the turn's tool calls all spawn), sleeps end at T0+3..T0+12.
- `waitForScreen(_allRunning, 60s)` — waits for "10 running".
- `waitForOutput(settleMs: 200)`.

If between two notices there's ≥500ms of silence, waitForOutput returns early. Sleeps are 1s apart, so with NO repaint noise in between, a 500ms window WILL expire between notices. But the countdown board repaints every... the countdown tick? The board shows "N running" which changes when a job finishes — that's event-driven, not a 1Hz tick. So between job 4 finishing at T+6 and job 5 at T+7, is there any other output? Probably not! So waitForOutput(settleMs: 500) would return at ~T+6.5s, with only 4 notices. That matches {1,2,3,4} exactly!

Hmm wait, but then this test would fail almost EVERY time... but it passes usually ("116 tests passed, 1 failed"). Something else must normally generate output. Key insight: `waitForOutput` returns the **accumulated raw buffer** (`_rawBuffer.toString()`), not just the last chunk. So `drained` contains everything from the whole session so far, and the regex matches all settle notices that have arrived. It returns when the raw buffer is unchanged for `settleMs` twice in a row (2 × 500ms = 1s of silence, checked at 500ms intervals).

So the failure mode: the raw stream went quiet for ~1s between settle notices. The ten jobs' settle notices arrive ~1s apart (sleep 3..12 staggered by 1s). The check: after each 500ms delay, compare buffer length. If unchanged twice consecutively → return. Between notice N (at T+N) and notice N+1 (at T+N+1): after the first 500ms sample the buffer is unchanged (stableTurns=1), after the second sample at T+N+1.0... the notice arrives at approximately exactly 1s after the previous — race! If the notice arrives just AFTER the second sample (i.e., gap > 1.0s from previous sample alignment), it returns with N notices.

Under load, sleeps fire at ≥ their nominal time, so gaps are ≥1s and jitter makes >1s gaps common → early return with a partial set. In the failing runs: {1,2,3,4} (returned ~T+6.5s) and {1..7} (returned ~T+9.5s).

Wait — but hold on: settle notices are delivered via "the async-result flow": each settled job spawns a settle-notice run which streams output. The turn loop is busy until the FIRST turn completes. Job finishes at T+3s.. — but if the agent turn is still streaming (until all ten tool calls are dispatched + result processing), the first notices may only appear after the turn completes. Regardless — the drain phase spans ~9s with notices ~1s apart, and waitForOutput(settleMs:500) needs 1s of silence to return; the gaps between notices are exactly ~1s, so the 2-sample check races the next notice. On a loaded runner, a notice can slip past the sample → early return.

Hmm, wait. Let me recheck: the while loop samples every `settleMs` (500ms). It breaks when `_rawBuffer.length == lastLength` for 2 consecutive samples. Timeline: notice at 6.0s, next at 7.0s. Samples at 6.0x, 6.5 (unchanged, stable=1), 7.0 (notice arrives at 7.001 → unchanged, stable=2 → BREAK). So yes — if the next notice lands in the second half of any 500ms sample boundary after ~2 samples, it returns early. Roughly: return happens at the first sample pair where both samples miss a notice; with notices 1s apart and samples 0.5s apart, the probability of catching 2 consecutive no-notice samples is high UNLESS other output (board repaints) keeps the buffer growing.

What normally keeps the buffer growing between notices? The board repaints each time a job finishes ("N running" changes). That's the same event. Also the "mid" wait loop — no.

Actually, ALSO: after the last turn ends, the board countdown rows repaint per second? Let me check the countdown tick — `_scheduleScheduledTick` was for scheduled rows. For shell jobs, the countdown might repaint per second (live countdown display "mm:ss" per job?). The card shows "10 running" etc. If each job row shows elapsed time ticking every second, frames repaint every second, producing output — keeping the buffer alive. Under load, a repaint can be delayed.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1290
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1290
- **Title**: fix(1252): widen scheduled-indicator reminder window past loaded-runner pre-check
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1252-followup-row-order` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +15
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:45:45Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T20:57:04Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1252

## Root cause (artifact-backed, FILE:LINE)
`test/integration/scheduled_indicator_test.dart` scripts a `schedule_message` with `delay: 20s`, then asserts the `⏰ 1 scheduled · next in` ETA inside a 10s `waitForScreen` that starts only after boot + scheduling turn + settle waits. On loaded CI runners that pre-check path measured **~44 s**: the CI dart-test JSON artifact of failing run 37223287603 (integration-json-shard-0) shows the test starting at suite-t=171.5 s and erroring at 225.5 s (54 s total), with the TimeoutException from `pty_harness.dart:377 waitForScreen` ← `scheduled_indicator_test.dart:64` (`· next in`). The failure screen already shows the complete fire→wake→deliver lifecycle (`[sched] fired:`, `[btw] mail → complete`, row cleared) — the record's 20 s pending window expired before the ETA check began sampling.

Product code audited and correct in all three artifacts: queue math (`scheduled_messages.dart` `dueMs`, `_armAsync` timer legs, boot re-arm via `start()`), sweep paths (`agent_cli_inbox.dart` `deliverDue` at boot/turn/wake), row renderer (`fa_tui_rows.dart:407 _scheduledRowLine`, epoch-millisecond ETA, minute-boundary repaint via `fa_tui.dart:819 _scheduleScheduledTick`). This is the same window-budget class as gh-1012; that fix's premise ("schedule → indicator → turn-complete tail is then a bounded ~2s") no longer holds on today's runners.

## Change (test-only, 15+/9−)
- Scripted reminder delay `20s` → `90s`: the pending window now dwarfs the worst observed pre-check path (~44 s) with ~2× headroom, so the `· next in` samples always land on a live record.
- Corrected the stale header comment (bounded-tail premise) and mock doc (said "3s delay"); documented the 44 s artifact measurement inline.
- All downstream budgets still line up: 10 s ETA wait samples ~46+ s before the fire; 90 s `[sched] fired:` wait covers the new fire point; 45 s clear poll and 5 m file timeout unchanged.

## Delivered vs remaining
- Delivered: window-budget fix + evidence-linked comments; no product code touched.
- Remaining: none known.

## Gates (disclosure)
Targeted `dart analyze` could not run on this box (shared Flutter SDK cache is read-only for the agent — wrapper fails before analyze starts; per lane policy the single attempt was spent, no dart test attempted — box runs a live LLM loop). Edits are string-literal/comment-only in one test file. **PR CI is the real gate.**

## Quarantine (`scripts/test_quarantine.json`)
Entry for this file/test **stays** in this PR, per gh-1199 AC4: the gate runs it supervised, nightly must produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof on the fixed code before removal (flakes are timing-dependent; a green repeat has not been produced yet). Please review/keep the entry as merged by #1249.

  "key": "pr-1290",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "fix(1252): widen scheduled-indicator reminder window past loaded-runner pre-check",
    "description": "Fixes #1252

## Root cause (artifact-backed, FILE:LINE)
`test/integration/scheduled_indicator_test.dart` scripts a `schedule_message` with `delay: 20s`, then asserts the `⏰ 1 scheduled · next in` ETA inside a 10s `waitForScreen` that starts only after boot + scheduling turn + settle waits. On loaded CI runners that pre-check path measured **~44 s**: the CI dart-test JSON artifact of failing run 37223287603 (integration-json-shard-0) shows the test starting at suite-t=171.5 s and erroring at 225.5 s (54 s total), with the TimeoutException from `pty_harness.dart:377 waitForScreen` ← `scheduled_indicator_test.dart:64` (`· next in`). The failure screen already shows the complete fire→wake→deliver lifecycle (`[sched] fired:`, `[btw] mail → complete`, row cleared) — the record's 20 s pending window expired before the ETA check began sampling.

Product code audited and correct in all three artifacts: queue math (`scheduled_messages.dart` `dueMs`, `_armAsync` timer legs, boot re-arm via `start()`), sweep paths (`agent_cli_inbox.dart` `deliverDue` at boot/turn/wake), row renderer (`fa_tui_rows.dart:407 _scheduledRowLine`, epoch-millisecond ETA, minute-boundary repaint via `fa_tui.dart:819 _scheduleScheduledTick`). This is the same window-budget class as gh-1012; that fix's premise ("schedule → indicator → turn-complete tail is then a bounded ~2s") no longer holds on today's runners.

## Change (test-only, 15+/9−)
- Scripted reminder delay `20s` → `90s`: the pending window now dwarfs the worst observed pre-check path (~44 s) with ~2× headroom, so the `· next in` samples always land on a live record.
- Corrected the stale header comment (bounded-tail premise) and mock doc (said "3s delay"); documented the 44 s artifact measurement inline.
- All downstream budgets still line up: 10 s ETA wait samples ~46+ s before the fire; 90 s `[sched] fired:` wait covers the new fire point; 45 s clear poll and 5 m file timeout unchanged.

## Delivered vs remaining
- Delivered: window-budget fix + evidence-linked comments; no product code touched.
- Remaining: none known.

## Gates (disclosure)
Targeted `dart analyze` could not run on this box (shared Flutter SDK cache is read-only for the agent — wrapper fails before analyze starts; per lane policy the single attempt was spent, no dart test attempted — box runs a live LLM loop). Edits are string-literal/comment-only in one test file. **PR CI is the real gate.**

## Quarantine (`scripts/test_quarantine.json`)
Entry for this file/test **stays** in this PR, per gh-1199 AC4: the gate runs it supervised, nightly must produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof on the fixed code before removal (flakes are timing-dependent; a green repeat has not been produced yet). Please review/keep the entry as merged by #1249."
  }
}

If the notice arrives just AFTER the second sample (i.e., gap > 1.0s from previous sample alignment), it returns with N notices.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1290
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1290
- **Title**: fix(1252): widen scheduled-indicator reminder window past loaded-runner pre-check
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1252-followup-row-order` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +15
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T12:45:45Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T20:57:04Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1252

## Root cause (artifact-backed, FILE:LINE)
`test/integration/scheduled_indicator_test.dart` scripts a `schedule_message` with `delay: 20s`, then asserts the `⏰ 1 scheduled · next in` ETA inside a 10s `waitForScreen` that starts only after boot + scheduling turn + settle waits. On loaded CI runners that pre-check path measured **~44 s**: the CI dart-test JSON artifact of failing run 37223287603 (integration-json-shard-0) shows the test starting at suite-t=171.5 s and erroring at 225.5 s (54 s total), with the TimeoutException from `pty_harness.dart:377 waitForScreen` ← `scheduled_indicator_test.dart:64` (`· next in`). The failure screen already shows the complete fire→wake→deliver lifecycle (`[sched] fired:`, `[btw] mail → complete`, row cleared) — the record's 20 s pending window expired before the ETA check began sampling.

Product code audited and correct in all three artifacts: queue math (`scheduled_messages.dart` `dueMs`, `_armAsync` timer legs, boot re-arm via `start()`), sweep paths (`agent_cli_inbox.dart` `deliverDue` at boot/turn/wake), row renderer (`fa_tui_rows.dart:407 _scheduledRowLine`, epoch-millisecond ETA, minute-boundary repaint via `fa_tui.dart:819 _scheduleScheduledTick`). This is the same window-budget class as gh-1012; that fix's premise ("schedule → indicator → turn-complete tail is then a bounded ~2s") no longer holds on today's runners.

## Change (test-only, 15+/9−)
- Scripted reminder delay `20s` → `90s`: the pending window now dwarfs the worst observed pre-check path (~44 s) with ~2× headroom, so the `· next in` samples always land on a live record.
- Corrected the stale header comment (bounded-tail premise) and mock doc (said "3s delay"); documented the 44 s artifact measurement inline.
- All downstream budgets still line up: 10 s ETA wait samples ~46+ s before the fire; 90 s `[sched] fired:` wait covers the new fire point; 45 s clear poll and 5 m file timeout unchanged.

## Delivered vs remaining
- Delivered: window-budget fix + evidence-linked comments; no product code touched.
- Remaining: none known.

## Gates (disclosure)
Targeted `dart analyze` could not run on this box (shared Flutter SDK cache is read-only for the agent — wrapper fails before analyze starts; per lane policy the single attempt was spent, no dart test attempted — box runs a live LLM loop). Edits are string-literal/comment-only in one test file. **PR CI is the real gate.**

## Quarantine (`scripts/test_quarantine.json`)
Entry for this file/test **stays** in this PR, per gh-1199 AC4: the gate runs it supervised, nightly must produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof on the fixed code before removal (flakes are timing-dependent; a green repeat has not been produced yet). Please review/keep the entry as merged by #1249.

blocks.text:
Now I understand the flake:

The test runs ten background bash jobs: `sleep ${2 + i} && echo p573-job-$i` for i=1..10, so sleeps are 3..12 seconds.

Then at line ~157:
```dart
final settledNumbers = _settleNotice
    .allMatches(drained)
    .map((m) => m.group(1)!.split('-').first)
    .toSet();
expect(
  settledNumbers,
  {for (var i = 1; i <= 10; i++) '$i'},
  ...
);
```

`_settleNotice = RegExp(r'\[bash\] sh-(\S+) exited\(0\)')` — matches `[bash] sh-<id> exited(0)` settle notices.

The failure: `settledNumbers` = {1,2,3,4} (missing 5..10) in run 37527310604, and {1..7} (missing 8,9,10) in run 37517510546.

So only the first 4 (or 7) jobs produced settle notices by the time `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500, timeout: 60s)` returned. Wait, but the timeout is 60s and jobs sleep 3..12s. How could only 4 finish in 60s? Unless `waitForOutput` returned early — it returns when output is "settled" (no new output for settleMs=500ms). Hmm, but settle notices keep streaming every ~1s as jobs finish (staggered 3..12s, so ~1s apart). If waitForOutput returns on a 500ms settle gap, it could return early between notices... but jobs finish ~1s apart, so there shouldn't be a 500ms gap...

Actually wait — look at the ordering: jobs launch staggered? All ten bash jobs launch essentially at the same time (10 tool calls in one turn). Sleeps: 3,4,5,...,12s. So finish events happen at ~3s, ~4s, ~5s, ..., ~12s — one per second. With settleMs: 500, waitForOutput would return only after a 500ms gap with no output... which never happens while jobs are finishing 1s apart. UNLESS output events are batched differently.

Hmm, but the failure shows waitForOutput returned after only 4 settle notices (t≈3,4,5,6 → returns at ~6.5s? Or the notices for 4 jobs). Under heavy CI load, jobs run slowly; sleeps don't depend on CPU though. BUT the notice delivery may be batched: the TUI delivers settle notices on frame repaints. If the terminal is busy, multiple notices could be coalesced into one frame and then... the regex captures distinct numbers; missing ones mean they never appeared in the drained stream.

Wait — actually, re-read the comment in the test:

"Frame repaints re-emit notices into the raw stream — the start/finish proof is the set of DISTINCT settled job numbers, not the raw match count."

So `drained` = the raw output stream chunk returned by waitForOutput. The notices are re-emitted on repaints. Missing numbers → the notices weren't emitted (yet) when waitForOutput returned.

Why would waitForOutput return before all 10 jobs finished? Because `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500)` returns when the output stream is quiet for 500ms. Between t=6s (job 4 done) and t=7s (job 5 done) there's a 1s gap... that's > 500ms! So waitForOutput CAN return in any of those ~1s gaps. That's exactly the bug: with staggered sleeps 3..12 (1s apart), the inter-notice gap is ~1s ≥ 500ms settle window, so `waitForOutput` can return after ANY notice, e.g. after the 4th.

Hmm wait, but then this test would be flaky by design... unless normally PTY output repaints keep the stream busy during the whole drain (status line repaints every second via countdown tick etc.). Key insight: `waitForOutput` returns the **accumulated raw buffer** (`_rawBuffer.toString()`), not just the last chunk. So `drained` contains everything from the whole session so far, and the regex matches all settle notices that have arrived. It returns when the raw buffer is unchanged for `settleMs` twice in a row (2 × 500ms = 1s of silence, checked at 500ms intervals).

So the failure mode: the raw stream went quiet for ~1s between settle notices. The ten jobs' settle notices arrive ~1s apart (sleep 3..12 staggered by 1s). The check: after each 500ms delay, compare buffer length. If unchanged twice consecutively → return. Between notice N (at T+N) and notice N+1 (at T+N+1): after the first 500ms sample the buffer is unchanged (stableTurns=1), after the second sample at T+N+1.0... the notice arrives at approximately exactly 1s after the previous — race! If the notice arrives just AFTER the second sample (i.e., gap > 1.0s from previous sample alignment), it returns with N notices.

Under load, sleeps fire at ≥ their nominal time, so gaps are ≥1s and jitter makes >1s gaps common → early return with a partial set. In the failing runs: {1,2,3,4} (returned ~T+6.5s) and {1..7} (returned ~T+9.5s).

Wait — but hold on: settle notices are delivered via "the async-result flow": each settled job spawns a settle-notice run which streams output. The turn loop is busy until the FIRST turn completes. Job finishes at T+3s.. — but if the agent turn is still streaming (until all ten tool calls are dispatched + result processing), the first notices may only appear after the turn completes. Regardless — the drain phase spans ~9s with notices ~1s apart, and waitForOutput(settleMs:500) needs 1s of silence to return; the gaps between notices are exactly ~1s, so the 2-sample check races the next notice. On a loaded runner, a notice can slip past the sample → early return.

Roughly: return happens at the first sample pair where both samples miss a notice; with notices 1s apart and samples 0.5s apart, the probability of catching 2 consecutive no-notice samples is high UNLESS other output (board repaints) keeps the buffer growing.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Apply the gh-1199 AC6 flake quarantine to a set of test targets.

Reads candidate test paths (one per line) from stdin, or as positional
arguments, and prints the paths that STAY in the gate to stdout. Files
listed in scripts/test_quarantine.json are dropped — with a `::warning::`
per skip, so the gate log always shows what the quarantine is shielding
(E3: a quarantine must never swallow a real regression silently).

Usage (the CI legs pipe their shard selection through it):

    python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json 0 \
        --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    find test/integration -name '*_test.dart' \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py --check
        validates the quarantine list itself: entries must reference
        existing files that are tagged `integration` and carry an issue
        link — a stale or under-documented entry fails the static gate.

The list is checked in and reviewed in the fix PR; flake_watch.py
(auto-filed flake issues) proposes entries with the proving runs attached.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on a malformed list or --check failure.
"""

import json
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from shard_files import file_has_tag

LIST_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),
                         "test_quarantine.json")

REQUIRED_FIELDS = ("file", "issue", "since", "runs")


def load_quarantine(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> list:
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        doc = json.load(f)
    entries = doc.get("quarantined")
    if not isinstance(entries, list):
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: 'quarantined' must be a list")
    return entries


def quarantined_files(entries: list) -> set:
    return {e["file"] for e in entries}


def check(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> int:
    """Validate the list; a stale/under-documented entry fails the gate."""
    ok = True
    try:
        entries = load_quarantine(path)

Now I understand the flake:

The test runs ten background bash jobs: `sleep ${2 + i} && echo p573-job-$i` for i=1..10, so sleeps are 3..12 seconds.

Then at line ~157:
```dart
final settledNumbers = _settleNotice
    .allMatches(drained)
    .map((m) => m.group(1)!.split('-').first)
    .toSet();
expect(
  settledNumbers,
  {for (var i = 1; i <= 10; i++) '$i'},
  ...
);
```

`_settleNotice = RegExp(r'\[bash\] sh-(\S+) exited\(0\)')` — matches `[bash] sh-<id> exited(0)` settle notices.

The failure: `settledNumbers` = {1,2,3,4} (missing 5..10) in run 37527310604, and {1..7} (missing 8,9,10) in run 37517510546.

So only the first 4 (or 7) jobs produced settle notices by the time `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500, timeout: 60s)` returned. Wait, but the timeout is 60s and jobs sleep 3..12s. How could only 4 finish in 60s? Unless `waitForOutput` returned early — it returns when output is "settled" (no new output for settleMs=500ms). Hmm, but settle notices keep streaming every ~1s as jobs finish (staggered 3..12s, so ~1s apart). If waitForOutput returns on a 500ms settle gap, it could return early between notices... but jobs finish ~1s apart, so there shouldn't be a 500ms gap...

Actually wait — look at the ordering: jobs launch staggered? All ten bash jobs launch essentially at the same time (10 tool calls in one turn). Sleeps: 3,4,5,...,12s. So finish events happen at ~3s, ~4s, ~5s, ..., ~12s — one per second. With settleMs: 500, waitForOutput would return only after a 500ms gap with no output... which never happens while jobs are finishing 1s apart. UNLESS output events are batched differently.

Hmm, but the failure shows waitForOutput returned after only 4 settle notices (t≈3,4,5,6 → returns at ~6.5s? Or the notices for 4 jobs). Under heavy CI load, jobs run slowly; sleeps don't depend on CPU though. BUT the notice delivery may be batched: the TUI delivers settle notices on frame repaints. If the terminal is busy, multiple notices could be coalesced into one frame and then... the regex captures distinct numbers; missing ones mean they never appeared in the drained stream.

Wait — actually, re-read the comment in the test:

"Frame repaints re-emit notices into the raw stream — the start/finish proof is the set of DISTINCT settled job numbers, not the raw match count."

So `drained` = the raw output stream chunk returned by waitForOutput. The notices are re-emitted on repaints. Missing numbers → the notices weren't emitted (yet) when waitForOutput returned.

Why would waitForOutput return before all 10 jobs finished? Because `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500)` returns when the output stream is quiet for 500ms. Between t=6s (job 4 done) and t=7s (job 5 done) there's a 1s gap... that's > 500ms! So waitForOutput CAN return in any of those ~1s gaps. That's exactly the bug: with staggered sleeps 3..12 (1s apart), the inter-notice gap is ~1s ≥ 500ms settle window, so `waitForOutput` can return after ANY notice, e.g. after the 4th.

Key insight: `waitForOutput` returns the **accumulated raw buffer** (`_rawBuffer.toString()`), not just the last chunk. So `drained` contains everything from the whole session so far, and the regex matches all settle notices that have arrived. It returns when the raw buffer is unchanged for `settleMs` twice in a row (2 × 500ms = 1s of silence, checked at 500ms intervals).

So the failure mode: the raw stream went quiet for ~1s between settle notices. The ten jobs' settle notices arrive ~1s apart (sleep 3..12 staggered by 1s). The check: after each 500ms delay, compare buffer length. If unchanged twice consecutively → return. Between notice N (at T+N) and notice N+1 (at T+N+1): after the first 500ms sample the buffer is unchanged (stableTurns=1), after the second sample at T+N+1.0... the notice arrives at approximately exactly 1s after the previous — race! If the notice arrives just AFTER the second sample (i.e., gap > 1.0s from previous sample alignment), it returns with N notices.

Under load, sleeps fire at ≥ their nominal time, so gaps are ≥1s and jitter makes >1s gaps common → early return with a partial set. In the failing runs: {1,2,3,4} (returned ~T+6.5s) and {1..7} (returned ~T+9.5s).

Wait — but hold on: settle notices are delivered via "the async-result flow": each settled job spawns a settle-notice run which streams output. The turn loop is busy until the FIRST turn completes. Job finishes at T+3s.. — but if the agent turn is still streaming (until all ten tool calls are dispatched + result processing), the first notices may only appear after the turn completes. Regardless — the drain phase spans ~9s with notices ~1s apart, and waitForOutput(settleMs:500) needs 1s of silence to return; the gaps between notices are exactly ~1s, so the 2-sample check races the next notice. On a loaded runner, a notice can slip past the sample → early return.

Hmm, wait. Let me recheck: the while loop samples every `settleMs` (500ms). It breaks when `_rawBuffer.length == lastLength` for 2 consecutive samples. Timeline: notice at 6.0s, next at 7.0s. Samples at 6.0x, 6.5 (unchanged, stable=1), 7.0 (notice arrives at 7.001 → unchanged, stable=2 → BREAK). So yes — if the next notice lands in the second half of any 500ms sample boundary after ~2 samples, it returns early. Roughly: return happens at the first sample pair where both samples miss a notice; with notices 1s apart and samples 0.5s apart, the probability of catching 2 consecutive no-notice samples is high UNLESS other output (board repaints) keeps the buffer growing.
