# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml. This
# file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


# The factory's own permissions block cannot raise rights above the
# caller, and the org default caps the token at read-only — the silent
# update-branch path (workflow token, updatePullRequestBranch) failed
# live with "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update
# this pull request" until this explicit block lifted the ceiling.
permissions:
  # contents: write — update-branch pushes a merge commit onto the PR head
  # branch; PullRequests: write alone is denied at the refs level (live:
  # "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update this pull
  # request" even with PullRequests: write granted).
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510):
                          # the reusable factory requests it — the caller
                          # must grant an equal-or-superset or the workflow
                          # dies with startup_failure (live 16:03-16:13 ×3).
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): awf main is load-bearing and review-gated, so
    # pack fixes go live on merge with no re-pin ceremony (recently
    # shipped on main: #579 conflict-rework, #577/#578
    # mutexExcludeSelf-by-fact-of-holding, #576 review-machine-unlinked,
    # #573-#574 pack snapshots + registry env, #572 review-stale-verdict,
    # #571 dmtools self-heal, #570 SM budget 1→3, #569 rework fatality,
    # #568 mergeBot workspace/repository args, #566 pack-registry runner
    # overrides). Accepted trade-off: a mutable ref executes whatever
    # sits at the awf main head at run start. The ENGINE (dmtools-agents)
    # resolves from releases via vars — no factory_ref here. Flip in
    # lockstep with the other machine-loop stubs — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: one source of truth for the machine login (repo variable).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping arrives empty.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
      # Dispatch-only CI: this repo's CI file (the SM dispatches it on PR
      # heads; default 'quality.yml' fits dmtools-dart, not this repo).
      ci-workflow: ci.yml
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — ci-gate.yml bridge is deleted in this PR.
      validation-checks: '["Quality gate","JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)","Binaries smoke gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"fa-state.json"}'
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares (SOURCE only) — mapping a
      # secret the callee does not declare is rejected at call time
      # (probe H2: +ZAI/KIMI => startup failure; probe I: exact set => green).
      # NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an
      # empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets
      # (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

messages.preview: The flake: ten staggered `sleep 3..12s` background jobs — settle notices land ~1s apart, and `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500)` can return in the inter-notice gap. Let me read the harness's `waitForOutput…

blocks.text:
Now I understand the flake:

The test runs ten background bash jobs: `sleep ${2 + i} && echo p573-job-$i` for i=1..10, so sleeps are 3..12 seconds.

Then at line ~157:
```dart
final settledNumbers = _settleNotice
    .allMatches(drained)
    .map((m) => m.group(1)!.split('-').first)
    .toSet();
expect(
  settledNumbers,
  {for (var i = 1; i <= 10; i++) '$i'},
  ...
);
```

`_settleNotice = RegExp(r'\[bash\] sh-(\S+) exited\(0\)')` — matches `[bash] sh-<id> exited(0)` settle notices.

The failure: `settledNumbers` = {1,2,3,4} (missing 5..10) in run 37527310604, and {1..7} (missing 8,9,10) in run 37517510546.

So only the first 4 (or 7) jobs produced settle notices by the time `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500, timeout: 60s)` returned. Wait, but the timeout is 60s and jobs sleep 3..12s. How could only 4 finish in 60s? Unless `waitForOutput` returned early — it returns when output is "settled" (no new output for settleMs=500ms). Hmm, but settle notices keep streaming every ~1s as jobs finish (staggered 3..12s, so ~1s apart). If waitForOutput returns on a 500ms settle gap, it could return early between notices... but jobs finish ~1s apart, so there shouldn't be a 500ms gap...

Actually wait — look at the ordering: jobs launch staggered? All ten bash jobs launch essentially at the same time (10 tool calls in one turn). Sleeps: 3,4,5,...,12s. So finish events happen at ~3s, ~4s, ~5s, ..., ~12s — one per second. With settleMs: 500, waitForOutput would return only after a 500ms gap with no output... which never happens while jobs are finishing 1s apart. UNLESS output events are batched differently.

Hmm, but the failure shows waitForOutput returned after only 4 settle notices (t≈3,4,5,6 → returns at ~6.5s? Or the notices for 4 jobs). Under heavy CI load, jobs run slowly; sleeps don't depend on CPU though. BUT the notice delivery may be batched: the TUI delivers settle notices on frame repaints. If the terminal is busy, multiple notices could be coalesced into one frame and then... the regex captures distinct numbers; missing ones mean they never appeared in the drained stream.

Wait — actually, re-read the comment in the test:

"Frame repaints re-emit notices into the raw stream — the start/finish proof is the set of DISTINCT settled job numbers, not the raw match count."

So `drained` = the raw output stream chunk returned by waitForOutput. The notices are re-emitted on repaints. Missing numbers → the notices weren't emitted (yet) when waitForOutput returned.

Why would waitForOutput return before all 10 jobs finished? Because `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500)` returns when the output stream is quiet for 500ms. Between t=6s (job 4 done) and t=7s (job 5 done) there's a 1s gap... that's > 500ms! So waitForOutput CAN return in any of those ~1s gaps. That's exactly the bug: with staggered sleeps 3..12 (1s apart), the inter-notice gap is ~1s ≥ 500ms settle window, so `waitForOutput` can return after ANY notice, e.g. after the 4th.

Hmm wait, but then this test would be flaky by design... unless normally PTY output repaints keep the stream busy during the whole drain (status line repaints every second via countdown tick etc.). Actually the board counts down each second (`9 running`, `8 running`...), which repaints frames, generating output. The settle notices themselves are emitted... let me think.

Actually the "0 running" wait later would still pass since drain completes by ~12s. And the settledNumbers set built from `drained` (just the final waitForOutput chunk?) — if the chunk only covers part of the drain, numbers missing.

Hold on — let me check `waitForOutput` in pty_harness.dart to understand exactly what it returns. Also, does it accumulate the whole stream or just the final chunk?

Also — the timing: in the failing CI run, the failure happened at 20:35:32, and the test group started at 20:35:13.7 (after lsp_dart_server_test at 20:35:13). So the failing test ran 20:34:57 → 20:35:32 (~35s) roughly. The ten sleeps take max 12s. Under load, more.

Key question: why did the drain stop after job 4? Look at the actual timeline:
- If the ten bash jobs start at T0 (after the turn's tool calls all spawn), sleeps end at T0+3..T0+12.
- `waitForScreen(_allRunning, 60s)` — waits for "10 running".
- `waitForOutput(settleMs: 200)`.
- mid-flight loop until a count in 1..9 appears (up to 60s).
- `waitForOutput(settleMs: 200)`.
- `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500, timeout: 60s)` → returns `drained` — this is the window where notices must all appear.

If between two notices there's ≥500ms of silence, waitForOutput returns early. Sleeps are 1s apart, so with NO repaint noise in between, a 500ms window WILL expire between notices. But the countdown board repaints every... the countdown tick? The board shows "N running" which changes when a job finishes — that's event-driven, not a 1Hz tick. So between job 4 finishing at T+6 and job 5 at T+7, is there any other output? Probably not! So waitForOutput(settleMs: 500) would return at ~T+6.5s, with only 4 notices. That matches {1,2,3,4} exactly!

Hmm wait, but then this test would fail almost EVERY time... but it passes usually ("116 tests passed, 1 failed"). Something else must normally generate output. Let me check waitForOutput's implementation — maybe it drains the ACCUMULATED stream since its last call, and the settle window starts from the last output... Let me read pty_harness.dart.

Also there's a "settle-notice run" — "A settle-notice run (the async-result flow) streams between settles — the board keeps counting down across runs." The turn ends, then settle notices for finished jobs spawn NEW runs ("[bash] sh-… exited(0)" as mail). Each settle notice triggers a new turn/run (the async-result flow). So after the main turn ends, each job finish triggers a run that streams the notice.

  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench
  harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run under supervision,

  scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path. A proven flake (red in ≥2
  distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h) is quarantined via

Key insight: `waitForOutput` returns the **accumulated raw buffer** (`_rawBuffer.toString()`), not just the last chunk. So `drained` contains everything from the whole session so far, and the regex matches all settle notices that have arrived. It returns when the raw buffer is unchanged for `settleMs` twice in a row (2 × 500ms = 1s of silence, checked at 500ms intervals).

So the failure mode: the raw stream went quiet for ~1s between settle notices. The ten jobs' settle notices arrive ~1s apart (sleep 3..12 staggered by 1s). The check: after each 500ms delay, compare buffer length. If unchanged twice consecutively → return. Between notice N (at T+N) and notice N+1 (at T+N+1): after the first 500ms sample the buffer is unchanged (stableTurns=1), after the second sample at T+N+1.0... the notice arrives at approximately exactly 1s after the previous — race! If the notice arrives just AFTER the second sample (i.e., gap > 1.0s from previous sample alignment), it returns with N notices.

Under load, sleeps fire at ≥ their nominal time, so gaps are ≥1s and jitter makes >1s gaps common → early return with a partial set. In the failing runs: {1,2,3,4} (returned ~T+6.5s) and {1..7} (returned ~T+9.5s).

Wait — but hold on: settle notices are delivered via "the async-result flow": each settled job spawns a settle-notice run which streams output. The turn loop is busy until the FIRST turn completes. Job finishes at T+3s.. — but if the agent turn is still streaming (until all ten tool calls are dispatched + result processing), the first notices may only appear after the turn completes. Regardless — the drain phase spans ~9s with notices ~1s apart, and waitForOutput(settleMs:500) needs 1s of silence to return; the gaps between notices are exactly ~1s, so the 2-sample check races the next notice. On a loaded runner, a notice can slip past the sample → early return.

Hmm, wait. Let me recheck: the while loop samples every `settleMs` (500ms). It breaks when `_rawBuffer.length == lastLength` for 2 consecutive samples. Timeline: notice at 6.0s, next at 7.0s. Samples at 6.0x, 6.5 (unchanged, stable=1), 7.0 (notice arrives at 7.001 → unchanged, stable=2 → BREAK). So yes — if the next notice lands in the second half of any 500ms sample boundary after ~2 samples, it returns early. Roughly: return happens at the first sample pair where both samples miss a notice; with notices 1s apart and samples 0.5s apart, the probability of catching 2 consecutive no-notice samples is high UNLESS other output (board repaints) keeps the buffer growing.

What normally keeps the buffer growing between notices? The board repaints each time a job finishes ("N running" changes). That's the same event. Also the "mid" wait loop — no.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Apply the gh-1199 AC6 flake quarantine to a set of test targets.

Reads candidate test paths (one per line) from stdin, or as positional
arguments, and prints the paths that STAY in the gate to stdout. Files
listed in scripts/test_quarantine.json are dropped — with a `::warning::`
per skip, so the gate log always shows what the quarantine is shielding
(E3: a quarantine must never swallow a real regression silently).

Usage (the CI legs pipe their shard selection through it):

    python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json 0 \
        --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    find test/integration -name '*_test.dart' \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py --check
        validates the quarantine list itself: entries must reference
        existing files that are tagged `integration` and carry an issue
        link — a stale or under-documented entry fails the static gate.

The list is checked in and reviewed in the fix PR; flake_watch.py
(auto-filed flake issues) proposes entries with the proving runs attached.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on a malformed list or --check failure.
"""

import json
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from shard_files import file_has_tag

LIST_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),
                         "test_quarantine.json")

REQUIRED_FIELDS = ("file", "issue", "since", "runs")


def load_quarantine(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> list:
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        doc = json.load(f)
    entries = doc.get("quarantined")
    if not isinstance(entries, list):
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: 'quarantined' must be a list")
    return entries


def quarantined_files(entries: list) -> set:
    return {e["file"] for e in entries}


def check(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> int:
    """Validate the list; a stale/under-documented entry fails the gate."""
    ok = True
    try:
        entries = load_quarantine(path)

# Machine SM — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (engine checkout, dmtools install, rule run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml. This
# file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


# The factory's own permissions block cannot raise rights above the
# caller, and the org default caps the token at read-only — the silent
# update-branch path (workflow token, updatePullRequestBranch) failed
# live with "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update
# this pull request" until this explicit block lifted the ceiling.
permissions:
  # contents: write — update-branch pushes a merge commit onto the PR head
  # branch; PullRequests: write alone is denied at the refs level (live:
  # "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update this pull
  # request" even with PullRequests: write granted).
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510):
                          # the reusable factory requests it — the caller
                          # must grant an equal-or-superset or the workflow
                          # dies with startup_failure (live 16:03-16:13 ×3).
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): awf main is load-bearing and review-gated, so
    # pack fixes go live on merge with no re-pin ceremony (recently
    # shipped on main: #579 conflict-rework, #577/#578
    # mutexExcludeSelf-by-fact-of-holding, #576 review-machine-unlinked,
    # #573-#574 pack snapshots + registry env, #572 review-stale-verdict,
    # #571 dmtools self-heal, #570 SM budget 1→3, #569 rework fatality,
    # #568 mergeBot workspace/repository args, #566 pack-registry runner
    # overrides). Accepted trade-off: a mutable ref executes whatever
    # sits at the awf main head at run start. The ENGINE (dmtools-agents)
    # resolves from releases via vars — no factory_ref here. Flip in
    # lockstep with the other machine-loop stubs — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: one source of truth for the machine login (repo variable).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping arrives empty.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
      # Dispatch-only CI: this repo's CI file (the SM dispatches it on PR
      # heads; default 'quality.yml' fits dmtools-dart, not this repo).
      ci-workflow: ci.yml
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — ci-gate.yml bridge is deleted in this PR.
      validation-checks: '["Quality gate","JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)","Binaries smoke gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"fa-state.json"}'
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares (SOURCE only) — mapping a
      # secret the callee does not declare is rejected at call time
      # (probe H2: +ZAI/KIMI => startup failure; probe I: exact set => green).
      # NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an
      # empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets
      # (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

messages.preview: The flake: ten staggered `sleep 3..12s` background jobs — settle notices land ~1s apart, and `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500)` can return in the inter-notice gap. Let me read the harness's `waitForOutput…

blocks.text:
Now I understand the flake:

The test runs ten background bash jobs: `sleep ${2 + i} && echo p573-job-$i` for i=1..10, so sleeps are 3..12 seconds.

Then at line ~157:
```dart
final settledNumbers = _settleNotice
    .allMatches(drained)
    .map((m) => m.group(1)!.split('-').first)
    .toSet();
expect(
  settledNumbers,
  {for (var i = 1; i <= 10; i++) '$i'},
  ...
);
```

`_settleNotice = RegExp(r'\[bash\] sh-(\S+) exited\(0\)')` — matches `[bash] sh-<id> exited(0)` settle notices.

The failure: `settledNumbers` = {1,2,3,4} (missing 5..10) in run 37527310604, and {1..7} (missing 8,9,10) in run 37517510546.

So only the first 4 (or 7) jobs produced settle notices by the time `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500, timeout: 60s)` returned. Wait, but the timeout is 60s and jobs sleep 3..12s. How could only 4 finish in 60s? Unless `waitForOutput` returned early — it returns when output is "settled" (no new output for settleMs=500ms). So the failure mode: the raw stream went quiet for ~1s between settle notices. The ten jobs' settle notices arrive ~1s apart (sleep 3..12 staggered by 1s). The check: after each 500ms delay, compare buffer length. If unchanged twice consecutively → return. Between notice N (at T+N) and notice N+1 (at T+N+1): after the first 500ms sample the buffer is unchanged (stableTurns=1), after the second sample at T+N+1.0... the notice arrives at approximately exactly 1s after the previous — race! If the notice arrives just AFTER the second sample (i.e., gap > 1.0s from previous sample alignment), it returns with N notices.

Under load, sleeps fire at ≥ their nominal time, so gaps are ≥1s and jitter makes >1s gaps common → early return with a partial set. In the failing runs: {1,2,3,4} (returned ~T+6.5s) and {1..7} (returned ~T+9.5s).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Apply the gh-1199 AC6 flake quarantine to a set of test targets.

Reads candidate test paths (one per line) from stdin, or as positional
arguments, and prints the paths that STAY in the gate to stdout. Files
listed in scripts/test_quarantine.json are dropped — with a `::warning::`
per skip, so the gate log always shows what the quarantine is shielding
(E3: a quarantine must never swallow a real regression silently).

Usage (the CI legs pipe their shard selection through it):

    python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json 0 \
        --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    find test/integration -name '*_test.dart' \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py --check
        validates the quarantine list itself: entries must reference
        existing files that are tagged `integration` and carry an issue
        link — a stale or under-documented entry fails the static gate.

The list is checked in and reviewed in the fix PR; flake_watch.py
(auto-filed flake issues) proposes entries with the proving runs attached.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on a malformed list or --check failure.
"""

import json
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from shard_files import file_has_tag

LIST_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),
                         "test_quarantine.json")

REQUIRED_FIELDS = ("file", "issue", "since", "runs")


def load_quarantine(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> list:
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        doc = json.load(f)
    entries = doc.get("quarantined")
    if not isinstance(entries, list):
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: 'quarantined' must be a list")
    return entries


def quarantined_files(entries: list) -> set:
    return {e["file"] for e in entries}


def check(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> int:
    """Validate the list; a stale/under-documented entry fails the gate."""
    ok = True
    try:
        entries = load_quarantine(path)

# Machine SM — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (engine checkout, dmtools install, rule run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml. This
# file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


# The factory's own permissions block cannot raise rights above the
# caller, and the org default caps the token at read-only — the silent
# update-branch path (workflow token, updatePullRequestBranch) failed
# live with "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update
# this pull request" until this explicit block lifted the ceiling.
permissions:
  # contents: write — update-branch pushes a merge commit onto the PR head
  # branch; PullRequests: write alone is denied at the refs level (live:
  # "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update this pull
  # request" even with PullRequests: write granted).
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510):
                          # the reusable factory requests it — the caller
                          # must grant an equal-or-superset or the workflow
                          # dies with startup_failure (live 16:03-16:13 ×3).
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): awf main is load-bearing and review-gated, so
    # pack fixes go live on merge with no re-pin ceremony (recently
    # shipped on main: #579 conflict-rework, #577/#578
    # mutexExcludeSelf-by-fact-of-holding, #576 review-machine-unlinked,
    # #573-#574 pack snapshots + registry env, #572 review-stale-verdict,
    # #571 dmtools self-heal, #570 SM budget 1→3, #569 rework fatality,
    # #568 mergeBot workspace/repository args, #566 pack-registry runner
    # overrides). Accepted trade-off: a mutable ref executes whatever
    # sits at the awf main head at run start. The ENGINE (dmtools-agents)
    # resolves from releases via vars — no factory_ref here. Flip in
    # lockstep with the other machine-loop stubs — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: one source of truth for the machine login (repo variable).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping arrives empty.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
      # Dispatch-only CI: this repo's CI file (the SM dispatches it on PR
      # heads; default 'quality.yml' fits dmtools-dart, not this repo).
      ci-workflow: ci.yml
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — ci-gate.yml bridge is deleted in this PR.
      validation-checks: '["Quality gate","JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)","Binaries smoke gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"fa-state.json"}'
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares (SOURCE only) — mapping a
      # secret the callee does not declare is rejected at call time
      # (probe H2: +ZAI/KIMI => startup failure; probe I: exact set => green).
      # NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an
      # empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets
      # (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

blocks.text:
Key insight: `waitForOutput` returns the **accumulated raw buffer** (`_rawBuffer.toString()`), not just the last chunk. So `drained` contains everything from the whole session so far, and the regex matches all settle notices that have arrived. It returns when the raw buffer is unchanged for `settleMs` twice in a row (2 × 500ms = 1s of silence, checked at 500ms intervals).

So the failure mode: the raw stream went quiet for ~1s between settle notices. The ten jobs' settle notices arrive ~1s apart (sleep 3..12 staggered by 1s). The check: after each 500ms delay, compare buffer length. If unchanged twice consecutively → return. Between notice N (at T+N) and notice N+1 (at T+N+1): after the first 500ms sample the buffer is unchanged (stableTurns=1), after the second sample at T+N+1.0... the notice arrives at approximately exactly 1s after the previous — race! If the notice arrives just AFTER the second sample (i.e., gap > 1.0s from previous sample alignment), it returns with N notices.

Under load, sleeps fire at ≥ their nominal time, so gaps are ≥1s and jitter makes >1s gaps common → early return with a partial set. In the failing runs: {1,2,3,4} (returned ~T+6.5s) and {1..7} (returned ~T+9.5s).

Wait — but hold on: settle notices are delivered via "the async-result flow": each settled job spawns a settle-notice run which streams output. The turn loop is busy until the FIRST turn completes. Job finishes at T+3s.. — but if the agent turn is still streaming (until all ten tool calls are dispatched + result processing), the first notices may only appear after the turn completes. Regardless — the drain phase spans ~9s with notices ~1s apart, and waitForOutput(settleMs:500) needs 1s of silence to return; the gaps between notices are exactly ~1s, so the 2-sample check races the next notice. On a loaded runner, a notice can slip past the sample → early return.

Hmm, wait. Let me recheck: the while loop samples every `settleMs` (500ms). It breaks when `_rawBuffer.length == lastLength` for 2 consecutive samples. Timeline: notice at 6.0s, next at 7.0s. Samples at 6.0x, 6.5 (unchanged, stable=1), 7.0 (notice arrives at 7.001 → unchanged, stable=2 → BREAK). So yes — if the next notice lands in the second half of any 500ms sample boundary after ~2 samples, it returns early. Roughly: return happens at the first sample pair where both samples miss a notice; with notices 1s apart and samples 0.5s apart, the probability of catching 2 consecutive no-notice samples is high UNLESS other output (board repaints) keeps the buffer growing.

What normally keeps the buffer growing between notices? The board repaints each time a job finishes ("N running" changes). That's the same event. Also the "mid" wait loop — no.

Actually, ALSO: after the last turn ends, the board countdown rows repaint per second? Let me check the countdown tick — `_scheduleScheduledTick` was for scheduled rows. For shell jobs, the countdown might repaint per second (live countdown display "mm:ss" per job?). The card shows "10 running" etc. If each job row shows elapsed time ticking every second, frames repaint every second, producing output — keeping the buffer alive. Under load, a repaint can be delayed.

OK. Regardless of exact mechanism, this is a timing-window flake of the same family as gh-1252/gh-1012/gh-1026: the drain-proof window (settleMs: 500 ⇒ 1s of silence) is not budgeted against the ~1s inter-notice spacing.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Apply the gh-1199 AC6 flake quarantine to a set of test targets.

Reads candidate test paths (one per line) from stdin, or as positional
arguments, and prints the paths that STAY in the gate to stdout. Files
listed in scripts/test_quarantine.json are dropped — with a `::warning::`
per skip, so the gate log always shows what the quarantine is shielding
(E3: a quarantine must never swallow a real regression silently).

Usage (the CI legs pipe their shard selection through it):

    python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json 0 \
        --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    find test/integration -name '*_test.dart' \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py --check
        validates the quarantine list itself: entries must reference
        existing files that are tagged `integration` and carry an issue
        link — a stale or under-documented entry fails the static gate.

The list is checked in and reviewed in the fix PR; flake_watch.py
(auto-filed flake issues) proposes entries with the proving runs attached.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on a malformed list or --check failure.
"""

import json
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from shard_files import file_has_tag

LIST_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),
                         "test_quarantine.json")

REQUIRED_FIELDS = ("file", "issue", "since", "runs")


def load_quarantine(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> list:
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        doc = json.load(f)
    entries = doc.get("quarantined")
    if not isinstance(entries, list):
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: 'quarantined' must be a list")
    return entries


def quarantined_files(entries: list) -> set:
    return {e["file"] for e in entries}


def check(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> int:
    """Validate the list; a stale/under-documented entry fails the gate."""
    ok = True
    try:
        entries = load_quarantine(path)

# Machine SM — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (engine checkout, dmtools install, rule run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml. This
# file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


# The factory's own permissions block cannot raise rights above the
# caller, and the org default caps the token at read-only — the silent
# update-branch path (workflow token, updatePullRequestBranch) failed
# live with "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update
# this pull request" until this explicit block lifted the ceiling.
permissions:
  # contents: write — update-branch pushes a merge commit onto the PR head
  # branch; PullRequests: write alone is denied at the refs level (live:
  # "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update this pull
  # request" even with PullRequests: write granted).
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510):
                          # the reusable factory requests it — the caller
                          # must grant an equal-or-superset or the workflow
                          # dies with startup_failure (live 16:03-16:13 ×3).
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): awf main is load-bearing and review-gated, so
    # pack fixes go live on merge with no re-pin ceremony (recently
    # shipped on main: #579 conflict-rework, #577/#578
    # mutexExcludeSelf-by-fact-of-holding, #576 review-machine-unlinked,
    # #573-#574 pack snapshots + registry env, #572 review-stale-verdict,
    # #571 dmtools self-heal, #570 SM budget 1→3, #569 rework fatality,
    # #568 mergeBot workspace/repository args, #566 pack-registry runner
    # overrides). Accepted trade-off: a mutable ref executes whatever
    # sits at the awf main head at run start. The ENGINE (dmtools-agents)
    # resolves from releases via vars — no factory_ref here. Flip in
    # lockstep with the other machine-loop stubs — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: one source of truth for the machine login (repo variable).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping arrives empty.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
      # Dispatch-only CI: this repo's CI file (the SM dispatches it on PR
      # heads; default 'quality.yml' fits dmtools-dart, not this repo).
      ci-workflow: ci.yml
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — ci-gate.yml bridge is deleted in this PR.
      validation-checks: '["Quality gate","JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)","Binaries smoke gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"fa-state.json"}'
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares (SOURCE only) — mapping a
      # secret the callee does not declare is rejected at call time
      # (probe H2: +ZAI/KIMI => startup failure; probe I: exact set => green).
      # NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an
      # empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets
      # (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

messages.preview: The flake: ten staggered `sleep 3..12s` background jobs — settle notices land ~1s apart, and `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500)` can return in the inter-notice gap. Let me read the harness's `waitForOutput…

blocks.text:
Now I understand the flake:

The test runs ten background bash jobs: `sleep ${2 + i} && echo p573-job-$i` for i=1..10, so sleeps are 3..12 seconds.

Then at line ~157:
```dart
final settledNumbers = _settleNotice
    .allMatches(drained)
    .map((m) => m.group(1)!.split('-').first)
    .toSet();
expect(
  settledNumbers,
  {for (var i = 1; i <= 10; i++) '$i'},
  ...
);
```

`_settleNotice = RegExp(r'\[bash\] sh-(\S+) exited\(0\)')` — matches `[bash] sh-<id> exited(0)` settle notices.

The failure: `settledNumbers` = {1,2,3,4} (missing 5..10) in run 37527310604, and {1..7} (missing 8,9,10) in run 37517510546.

So only the first 4 (or 7) jobs produced settle notices by the time `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500, timeout: 60s)` returned. Wait, but the timeout is 60s and jobs sleep 3..12s. How could only 4 finish in 60s? Unless `waitForOutput` returned early — it returns when output is "settled" (no new output for settleMs=500ms). Hmm, but settle notices keep streaming every ~1s as jobs finish (staggered 3..12s, so ~1s apart). If waitForOutput returns on a 500ms settle gap, it could return early between notices... but jobs finish ~1s apart, so there shouldn't be a 500ms gap...

Actually wait — look at the ordering: jobs launch staggered? All ten bash jobs launch essentially at the same time (10 tool calls in one turn). Sleeps: 3,4,5,...,12s. So finish events happen at ~3s, ~4s, ~5s, ..., ~12s — one per second. With settleMs: 500, waitForOutput would return only after a 500ms gap with no output... which never happens while jobs are finishing 1s apart. UNLESS output events are batched differently.

Hmm, but the failure shows waitForOutput returned after only 4 settle notices (t≈3,4,5,6 → returns at ~6.5s? Or the notices for 4 jobs). Under heavy CI load, jobs run slowly; sleeps don't depend on CPU though. BUT the notice delivery may be batched: the TUI delivers settle notices on frame repaints. If the terminal is busy, multiple notices could be coalesced into one frame and then... the regex captures distinct numbers; missing ones mean they never appeared in the drained stream.

Wait — actually, re-read the comment in the test:

"Frame repaints re-emit notices into the raw stream — the start/finish proof is the set of DISTINCT settled job numbers, not the raw match count."

So `drained` = the raw output stream chunk returned by waitForOutput. The notices are re-emitted on repaints. Missing numbers → the notices weren't emitted (yet) when waitForOutput returned.

Why would waitForOutput return before all 10 jobs finished? Because `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500)` returns when the output stream is quiet for 500ms. Between t=6s (job 4 done) and t=7s (job 5 done) there's a 1s gap... that's > 500ms! So waitForOutput CAN return in any of those ~1s gaps. That's exactly the bug: with staggered sleeps 3..12 (1s apart), the inter-notice gap is ~1s ≥ 500ms settle window, so `waitForOutput` can return after ANY notice, e.g. after the 4th.

Hmm wait, but then this test would be flaky by design... unless normally PTY output repaints keep the stream busy during the whole drain (status line repaints every second via countdown tick etc.). Actually the board counts down each second (`9 running`, `8 running`...), which repaints frames, generating output. The settle notices themselves are emitted... let me think.

Actually the "0 running" wait later would still pass since drain completes by ~12s. And the settledNumbers set built from `drained` (just the final waitForOutput chunk?) — if the chunk only covers part of the drain, numbers missing.

Hold on — let me check `waitForOutput` in pty_harness.dart to understand exactly what it returns. Also, does it accumulate the whole stream or just the final chunk?

Also — the timing: in the failing CI run, the failure happened at 20:35:32, and the test group started at 20:35:13.7 (after lsp_dart_server_test at 20:35:13). So the failing test ran 20:34:57 → 20:35:32 (~35s) roughly. The ten sleeps take max 12s. Under load, more.

Key question: why did the drain stop after job 4? Look at the actual timeline:
- If the ten bash jobs start at T0 (after the turn's tool calls all spawn), sleeps end at T0+3..T0+12.
- `waitForScreen(_allRunning, 60s)` — waits for "10 running".
- `waitForOutput(settleMs: 200)`.
- mid-flight loop until a count in 1..9 appears (up to 60s).
- `waitForOutput(settleMs: 200)`.
- `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500, timeout: 60s)` → returns `drained` — this is the window where notices must all appear.

If between two notices there's ≥500ms of silence, waitForOutput returns early. Sleeps are 1s apart, so with NO repaint noise in between, a 500ms window WILL expire between notices. But the countdown board repaints every... the countdown tick? The board shows "N running" which changes when a job finishes — that's event-driven, not a 1Hz tick. So between job 4 finishing at T+6 and job 5 at T+7, is there any other output? Probably not! So waitForOutput(settleMs: 500) would return at ~T+6.5s, with only 4 notices. That matches {1,2,3,4} exactly!

Hmm wait, but then this test would fail almost EVERY time... but it passes usually ("116 tests passed, 1 failed"). Something else must normally generate output. Let me check waitForOutput's implementation — maybe it drains the ACCUMULATED stream since its last call, and the settle window starts from the last output... Let me read pty_harness.dart.

Also there's a "settle-notice run" — "A settle-notice run (the async-result flow) streams between settles — the board keeps counting down across runs." The turn ends, then settle notices for finished jobs spawn NEW runs ("[bash] sh-… exited(0)" as mail). Each settle notice triggers a new turn/run (the async-result flow). So after the main turn ends, each job finish triggers a run that streams the notice.

Let me read the harness and understand. Then check whether there's a known fix approach — maybe gh-1337 issue was auto-filed for v1.0.520's red, and a fix is expected in this rework? - `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a

  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench
  harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run under supervision,
  plus manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging — NO
  scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path. A proven flake (red in ≥2
  distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h) is quarantined via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json` (checked in, reviewed in the fix PR;
  `flake-watch.yml` files the issue and opens the PR) — the gate legs pipe

Key insight: `waitForOutput` returns the **accumulated raw buffer** (`_rawBuffer.toString()`), not just the last chunk. So `drained` contains everything from the whole session so far, and the regex matches all settle notices that have arrived. It returns when the raw buffer is unchanged for `settleMs` twice in a row (2 × 500ms = 1s of silence, checked at 500ms intervals).

So the failure mode: the raw stream went quiet for ~1s between settle notices. The ten jobs' settle notices arrive ~1s apart (sleep 3..12 staggered by 1s). The check: after each 500ms delay, compare buffer length. If unchanged twice consecutively → return. Between notice N (at T+N) and notice N+1 (at T+N+1): after the first 500ms sample the buffer is unchanged (stableTurns=1), after the second sample at T+N+1.0... the notice arrives at approximately exactly 1s after the previous — race! If the notice arrives just AFTER the second sample (i.e., gap > 1.0s from previous sample alignment), it returns with N notices.

Under load, sleeps fire at ≥ their nominal time, so gaps are ≥1s and jitter makes >1s gaps common → early return with a partial set. In the failing runs: {1,2,3,4} (returned ~T+6.5s) and {1..7} (returned ~T+9.5s).

Wait — but hold on: settle notices are delivered via "the async-result flow": each settled job spawns a settle-notice run which streams output. The turn loop is busy until the FIRST turn completes. Job finishes at T+3s.. — but if the agent turn is still streaming (until all ten tool calls are dispatched + result processing), the first notices may only appear after the turn completes. Regardless — the drain phase spans ~9s with notices ~1s apart, and waitForOutput(settleMs:500) needs 1s of silence to return; the gaps between notices are exactly ~1s, so the 2-sample check races the next notice. On a loaded runner, a notice can slip past the sample → early return.

Hmm, wait. Let me recheck: the while loop samples every `settleMs` (500ms). It breaks when `_rawBuffer.length == lastLength` for 2 consecutive samples. Timeline: notice at 6.0s, next at 7.0s. Samples at 6.0x, 6.5 (unchanged, stable=1), 7.0 (notice arrives at 7.001 → unchanged, stable=2 → BREAK). So yes — if the next notice lands in the second half of any 500ms sample boundary after ~2 samples, it returns early. Roughly: return happens at the first sample pair where both samples miss a notice; with notices 1s apart and samples 0.5s apart, the probability of catching 2 consecutive no-notice samples is high UNLESS other output (board repaints) keeps the buffer growing.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Apply the gh-1199 AC6 flake quarantine to a set of test targets.

Reads candidate test paths (one per line) from stdin, or as positional
arguments, and prints the paths that STAY in the gate to stdout. Files
listed in scripts/test_quarantine.json are dropped — with a `::warning::`
per skip, so the gate log always shows what the quarantine is shielding
(E3: a quarantine must never swallow a real regression silently).

Usage (the CI legs pipe their shard selection through it):

    python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json 0 \
        --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    find test/integration -name '*_test.dart' \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py --check
        validates the quarantine list itself: entries must reference
        existing files that are tagged `integration` and carry an issue
        link — a stale or under-documented entry fails the static gate.

The list is checked in and reviewed in the fix PR; flake_watch.py
(auto-filed flake issues) proposes entries with the proving runs attached.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on a malformed list or --check failure.
"""

import json
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from shard_files import file_has_tag

LIST_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),
                         "test_quarantine.json")

REQUIRED_FIELDS = ("file", "issue", "since", "runs")


def load_quarantine(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> list:
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        doc = json.load(f)
    entries = doc.get("quarantined")
    if not isinstance(entries, list):
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: 'quarantined' must be a list")
    return entries


def quarantined_files(entries: list) -> set:
    return {e["file"] for e in entries}


def check(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> int:
    """Validate the list; a stale/under-documented entry fails the gate."""
    ok = True
    try:
        entries = load_quarantine(path)

# Machine SM — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (engine checkout, dmtools install, rule run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml. This
# file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


# The factory's own permissions block cannot raise rights above the
# caller, and the org default caps the token at read-only — the silent
# update-branch path (workflow token, updatePullRequestBranch) failed
# live with "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update
# this pull request" until this explicit block lifted the ceiling.
permissions:
  # contents: write — update-branch pushes a merge commit onto the PR head
  # branch; PullRequests: write alone is denied at the refs level (live:
  # "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update this pull
  # request" even with PullRequests: write granted).
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510):
                          # the reusable factory requests it — the caller
                          # must grant an equal-or-superset or the workflow
                          # dies with startup_failure (live 16:03-16:13 ×3).
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): awf main is load-bearing and review-gated, so
    # pack fixes go live on merge with no re-pin ceremony (recently
    # shipped on main: #579 conflict-rework, #577/#578
    # mutexExcludeSelf-by-fact-of-holding, #576 review-machine-unlinked,
    # #573-#574 pack snapshots + registry env, #572 review-stale-verdict,
    # #571 dmtools self-heal, #570 SM budget 1→3, #569 rework fatality,
    # #568 mergeBot workspace/repository args, #566 pack-registry runner
    # overrides). Accepted trade-off: a mutable ref executes whatever
    # sits at the awf main head at run start. The ENGINE (dmtools-agents)
    # resolves from releases via vars — no factory_ref here. Flip in
    # lockstep with the other machine-loop stubs — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: one source of truth for the machine login (repo variable).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping arrives empty.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
      # Dispatch-only CI: this repo's CI file (the SM dispatches it on PR
      # heads; default 'quality.yml' fits dmtools-dart, not this repo).
      ci-workflow: ci.yml
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — ci-gate.yml bridge is deleted in this PR.
      validation-checks: '["Quality gate","JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)","Binaries smoke gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"fa-state.json"}'
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares (SOURCE only) — mapping a
      # secret the callee does not declare is rejected at call time
      # (probe H2: +ZAI/KIMI => startup failure; probe I: exact set => green).
      # NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an
      # empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets
      # (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

messages.preview: The flake: ten staggered `sleep 3..12s` background jobs — settle notices land ~1s apart, and `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500)` can return in the inter-notice gap. Let me read the harness's `waitForOutput…

blocks.text:
Now I understand the flake:

The test runs ten background bash jobs: `sleep ${2 + i} && echo p573-job-$i` for i=1..10, so sleeps are 3..12 seconds.

Then at line ~157:
```dart
final settledNumbers = _settleNotice
    .allMatches(drained)
    .map((m) => m.group(1)!.split('-').first)
    .toSet();
expect(
  settledNumbers,
  {for (var i = 1; i <= 10; i++) '$i'},
  ...
);
```

`_settleNotice = RegExp(r'\[bash\] sh-(\S+) exited\(0\)')` — matches `[bash] sh-<id> exited(0)` settle notices.

The failure: `settledNumbers` = {1,2,3,4} (missing 5..10) in run 37527310604, and {1..7} (missing 8,9,10) in run 37517510546.

So only the first 4 (or 7) jobs produced settle notices by the time `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500, timeout: 60s)` returned. Wait, but the timeout is 60s and jobs sleep 3..12s. How could only 4 finish in 60s? Unless `waitForOutput` returned early — it returns when output is "settled" (no new output for settleMs=500ms). Hmm, but settle notices keep streaming every ~1s as jobs finish (staggered 3..12s, so ~1s apart). If waitForOutput returns on a 500ms settle gap, it could return early between notices... but jobs finish ~1s apart, so there shouldn't be a 500ms gap...

Actually wait — look at the ordering: jobs launch staggered? All ten bash jobs launch essentially at the same time (10 tool calls in one turn). Sleeps: 3,4,5,...,12s. So finish events happen at ~3s, ~4s, ~5s, ..., ~12s — one per second. With settleMs: 500, waitForOutput would return only after a 500ms gap with no output... which never happens while jobs are finishing 1s apart. UNLESS output events are batched differently.

Hmm, but the failure shows waitForOutput returned after only 4 settle notices (t≈3,4,5,6 → returns at ~6.5s? Or the notices for 4 jobs). Under heavy CI load, jobs run slowly; sleeps don't depend on CPU though. BUT the notice delivery may be batched: the TUI delivers settle notices on frame repaints. If the terminal is busy, multiple notices could be coalesced into one frame and then... the regex captures distinct numbers; missing ones mean they never appeared in the drained stream.

Wait — actually, re-read the comment in the test:

"Frame repaints re-emit notices into the raw stream — the start/finish proof is the set of DISTINCT settled job numbers, not the raw match count."

So `drained` = the raw output stream chunk returned by waitForOutput. The notices are re-emitted on repaints. Missing numbers → the notices weren't emitted (yet) when waitForOutput returned.

Why would waitForOutput return before all 10 jobs finished? Because `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500)` returns when the output stream is quiet for 500ms. Between t=6s (job 4 done) and t=7s (job 5 done) there's a 1s gap... that's > 500ms! So waitForOutput CAN return in any of those ~1s gaps. That's exactly the bug: with staggered sleeps 3..12 (1s apart), the inter-notice gap is ~1s ≥ 500ms settle window, so `waitForOutput` can return after ANY notice, e.g. after the 4th.

Hmm wait, but then this test would be flaky by design... unless normally PTY output repaints keep the stream busy during the whole drain (status line repaints every second via countdown tick etc.). Actually the board counts down each second (`9 running`, `8 running`...), which repaints frames, generating output. The settle notices themselves are emitted... let me think.

Actually the "0 running" wait later would still pass since drain completes by ~12s. And the settledNumbers set built from `drained` (just the final waitForOutput chunk?) — if the chunk only covers part of the drain, numbers missing.

Hold on — let me check `waitForOutput` in pty_harness.dart to understand exactly what it returns. Also, does it accumulate the whole stream or just the final chunk?

Also — the timing: in the failing CI run, the failure happened at 20:35:32, and the test group started at 20:35:13.7 (after lsp_dart_server_test at 20:35:13). So the failing test ran 20:34:57 → 20:35:32 (~35s) roughly. The ten sleeps take max 12s. Under load, more.

Key question: why did the drain stop after job 4? Look at the actual timeline:
- If the ten bash jobs start at T0 (after the turn's tool calls all spawn), sleeps end at T0+3..T0+12.
- `waitForScreen(_allRunning, 60s)` — waits for "10 running".
- `waitForOutput(settleMs: 200)`.
- mid-flight loop until a count in 1..9 appears (up to 60s).
- `waitForOutput(settleMs: 200)`.
- `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500, timeout: 60s)` → returns `drained` — this is the window where notices must all appear.

If between two notices there's ≥500ms of silence, waitForOutput returns early. Sleeps are 1s apart, so with NO repaint noise in between, a 500ms window WILL expire between notices. But the countdown board repaints every... the countdown tick? The board shows "N running" which changes when a job finishes — that's event-driven, not a 1Hz tick. So between job 4 finishing at T+6 and job 5 at T+7, is there any other output? Probably not! So waitForOutput(settleMs: 500) would return at ~T+6.5s, with only 4 notices. That matches {1,2,3,4} exactly!

Hmm wait, but then this test would fail almost EVERY time... but it passes usually ("116 tests passed, 1 failed"). Something else must normally generate output. Let me check waitForOutput's implementation — maybe it drains the ACCUMULATED stream since its last call, and the settle window starts from the last output... Let me read pty_harness.dart.

Also there's a "settle-notice run" — "A settle-notice run (the async-result flow) streams between settles — the board keeps counting down across runs." The turn ends, then settle notices for finished jobs spawn NEW runs ("[bash] sh-… exited(0)" as mail). Each settle notice triggers a new turn/run (the async-result flow). So after the main turn ends, each job finish triggers a run that streams the notice.

Let me read the harness and understand. Then check whether there's a known fix approach — maybe gh-1337 issue was auto-filed for v1.0.520's red, and a fix is expected in this rework? Key insight: `waitForOutput` returns the **accumulated raw buffer** (`_rawBuffer.toString()`), not just the last chunk. So `drained` contains everything from the whole session so far, and the regex matches all settle notices that have arrived. It returns when the raw buffer is unchanged for `settleMs` twice in a row (2 × 500ms = 1s of silence, checked at 500ms intervals).

So the failure mode: the raw stream went quiet for ~1s between settle notices. The ten jobs' settle notices arrive ~1s apart (sleep 3..12 staggered by 1s). The check: after each 500ms delay, compare buffer length. If unchanged twice consecutively → return. Between notice N (at T+N) and notice N+1 (at T+N+1): after the first 500ms sample the buffer is unchanged (stableTurns=1), after the second sample at T+N+1.0... the notice arrives at approximately exactly 1s after the previous — race! If the notice arrives just AFTER the second sample (i.e., gap > 1.0s from previous sample alignment), it returns with N notices.

Under load, sleeps fire at ≥ their nominal time, so gaps are ≥1s and jitter makes >1s gaps common → early return with a partial set. In the failing runs: {1,2,3,4} (returned ~T+6.5s) and {1..7} (returned ~T+9.5s).

Wait — but hold on: settle notices are delivered via "the async-result flow": each settled job spawns a settle-notice run which streams output. The turn loop is busy until the FIRST turn completes. Job finishes at T+3s.. — but if the agent turn is still streaming (until all ten tool calls are dispatched + result processing), the first notices may only appear after the turn completes. Regardless — the drain phase spans ~9s with notices ~1s apart, and waitForOutput(settleMs:500) needs 1s of silence to return; the gaps between notices are exactly ~1s, so the 2-sample check races the next notice. On a loaded runner, a notice can slip past the sample → early return.

Hmm, wait. Let me recheck: the while loop samples every `settleMs` (500ms). It breaks when `_rawBuffer.length == lastLength` for 2 consecutive samples. Timeline: notice at 6.0s, next at 7.0s. Samples at 6.0x, 6.5 (unchanged, stable=1), 7.0 (notice arrives at 7.001 → unchanged, stable=2 → BREAK). So yes — if the next notice lands in the second half of any 500ms sample boundary after ~2 samples, it returns early. Roughly: return happens at the first sample pair where both samples miss a notice; with notices 1s apart and samples 0.5s apart, the probability of catching 2 consecutive no-notice samples is high UNLESS other output (board repaints) keeps the buffer growing.

What normally keeps the buffer growing between notices? The board repaints each time a job finishes ("N running" changes). That's the same event. Also the "mid" wait loop — no.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Apply the gh-1199 AC6 flake quarantine to a set of test targets.

Reads candidate test paths (one per line) from stdin, or as positional
arguments, and prints the paths that STAY in the gate to stdout. Files
listed in scripts/test_quarantine.json are dropped — with a `::warning::`
per skip, so the gate log always shows what the quarantine is shielding
(E3: a quarantine must never swallow a real regression silently).

Usage (the CI legs pipe their shard selection through it):

    python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json 0 \
        --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    find test/integration -name '*_test.dart' \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py --check
        validates the quarantine list itself: entries must reference
        existing files that are tagged `integration` and carry an issue
        link — a stale or under-documented entry fails the static gate.

The list is checked in and reviewed in the fix PR; flake_watch.py
(auto-filed flake issues) proposes entries with the proving runs attached.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on a malformed list or --check failure.
"""

import json
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from shard_files import file_has_tag

LIST_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),
                         "test_quarantine.json")

REQUIRED_FIELDS = ("file", "issue", "since", "runs")


def load_quarantine(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> list:
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        doc = json.load(f)
    entries = doc.get("quarantined")
    if not isinstance(entries, list):
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: 'quarantined' must be a list")
    return entries


def quarantined_files(entries: list) -> set:
    return {e["file"] for e in entries}


def check(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> int:
    """Validate the list; a stale/under-documented entry fails the gate."""
    ok = True
    try:
        entries = load_quarantine(path)

# Machine SM — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (engine checkout, dmtools install, rule run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml. This
# file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


# The factory's own permissions block cannot raise rights above the
# caller, and the org default caps the token at read-only — the silent
# update-branch path (workflow token, updatePullRequestBranch) failed
# live with "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update
# this pull request" until this explicit block lifted the ceiling.
permissions:
  # contents: write — update-branch pushes a merge commit onto the PR head
  # branch; PullRequests: write alone is denied at the refs level (live:
  # "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update this pull
  # request" even with PullRequests: write granted).
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510):
                          # the reusable factory requests it — the caller
                          # must grant an equal-or-superset or the workflow
                          # dies with startup_failure (live 16:03-16:13 ×3).
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): awf main is load-bearing and review-gated, so
    # pack fixes go live on merge with no re-pin ceremony (recently
    # shipped on main: #579 conflict-rework, #577/#578
    # mutexExcludeSelf-by-fact-of-holding, #576 review-machine-unlinked,
    # #573-#574 pack snapshots + registry env, #572 review-stale-verdict,
    # #571 dmtools self-heal, #570 SM budget 1→3, #569 rework fatality,
    # #568 mergeBot workspace/repository args, #566 pack-registry runner
    # overrides). Accepted trade-off: a mutable ref executes whatever
    # sits at the awf main head at run start. The ENGINE (dmtools-agents)
    # resolves from releases via vars — no factory_ref here. Flip in
    # lockstep with the other machine-loop stubs — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: one source of truth for the machine login (repo variable).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping arrives empty.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
      # Dispatch-only CI: this repo's CI file (the SM dispatches it on PR
      # heads; default 'quality.yml' fits dmtools-dart, not this repo).
      ci-workflow: ci.yml
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — ci-gate.yml bridge is deleted in this PR.
      validation-checks: '["Quality gate","JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)","Binaries smoke gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"fa-state.json"}'
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares (SOURCE only) — mapping a
      # secret the callee does not declare is rejected at call time
      # (probe H2: +ZAI/KIMI => startup failure; probe I: exact set => green).
      # NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an
      # empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets
      # (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
